I'm telling you, I had the largest spider I've ever seen in my house last week. It was huge, at least an inch in diameter. I was terrified. Oh, blimey! That does sound big. What did you do? ...and then I found out that my great-great-grandfather was a blacksmith in Dorchester. Isn't that fascinating? I had no idea. Oh, that's wonderful! I've always been interested in family history. Ah'm tellin' ye, pet, that new film based on Jane Austen's novel is a must-see! The cinematography is stunning, and the cast is spot on. Ah loved the way they brought the characters to life. Alright, kids, settle down. I want to tell you a story about when I was a little girl. We didn't have all these fancy computers and games like you do now. We had to use our imaginations to have fun. Excel is a bit complicated for now. But I can teach you some basic things about computers if you want. Yeah! Teach us, Mummy! It's a great way to learn new things and make new friends. Can we talk about the Brownie Promise some more, Mummy? I didn't understand what some of the words meant.

Ah'm tellin' thee, John, Ah've had enough of these youngsters wearin' scruffy clothes everywhere they go. What's wrong wi' puttin' on a decent pair of trousers and a shirt, eh? Ah, come on, Margaret! You can't expect them to dress up like we used to back in the day. Times have changed, and so has fashion. Besides, they're probably more concerned with comfort than style. This one you've made is lovely, by the way – the eggs are cooked just right. Thanks, John! Ah put a bit of effort into it, even made some fresh jam from the fruit we picked up at that farm near Skipton last weekend. You know, the one wi' the beautiful views of the Dales? Ah yes, that sounds familiar! We used to go to a place like that near Windsor when I was a lad. They had the most wonderful fruit farms, and my parents would always take me and my siblings to pick our own strawberries and raspberries. And after that, we'd often go for a walk in the nearby woods and stumble upon old, deserted medieval villages. Fascinatin' places, full of history. Ooh, that sounds like a grand day out! Ah've always been fascinated by those old villages myself. There's sommat about the atmosphere, like you can almost hear the whispers of the past. Anyway, enough about that – have you seen the state of the roads around here lately? All these roadworks are causin' chaos! Ah had to take a detour just to get to the shops yesterday. Ah, yes! I've been caught out by those roadworks a time or two myself. But at least they're doin' sommat to improve the infrastructure, eh?

I'm telling you, I had the most wonderful Christmas dinner at my sister's this year. Her roast beef was just perfect, and the gravy was to die for. I've been thinking of trying out her recipe for our New Year's Eve party. Ah, that sounds lovely, dear. I'm sure you'll do it justice. By the way, have you taken your medication for the day? I'm so glad we're finally catching up, it feels like it's been ages. How's life as a postgrad student treating you? It's been keeping me busy, that's for sure. I completely agree. It's like, we're supposed to be one of the wealthiest countries in the world, but there are still people struggling to make ends meet. It's just not right. Exactly! I'm telling you, I've been trying to get back into exercising regularly, but it's just so hard to find the time. Between work and everything else, I feel like I'm always playing catch-up. I know what you mean. I've been trying to get to the gym more often, but it's tough. Although, I did manage to get out for a run on Sunday, so that was a bonus. You two and your exercising. Oh, don't even get me started. We were looking at moving to a bigger place, but the prices are just ridiculous. I mean, I know it's always been expensive around here, but it seems like it's getting worse and worse. I think it's a national problem, to be honest. And it's not just the prices, it's the state of the houses themselves. I've seen some of the places that are on the market, and they're just dumpers. You'd need to spend a fortune just to get them livable. Dumpers, that's a good one. But, yeah, it's true. We looked at this one place, and it was like they hadn't updated it since the 70s. I mean, I like a bit of character, but this was just old and rundown. So, what's the plan, then? Are you guys going to keep looking, or are you just going to stay put? I think we're going to keep looking, but we're being picky. We don't want to settle for something that's not right. And, in the meantime, I'm just going to have to get used to living in a tiny kitchen. Speaking of which, has anyone got any good cooking tips? I'm getting so bored with the same old recipes. Oh, actually, I was just reading this cookbook the other day, and it had some great ideas for quick and easy meals. I was thinking of trying out this one recipe for chicken and rice...

Alrigh' then, how's work goin' for ye? I feel like I haven't seen ye in ages, an' we're sittin' here in this lovely Botanic Gardens in Cambridge, enjoying the scenery. Ah, it's been keepin' me busy, to be honest. Just finished a big project, and now I'm workin' on a new one. You know how it is. But I did manage to catch up on the news about the Budget. Have you had a chance to look into it? Aye, I had a glance. I'm not exactly sure what to make of it, though. All these figures an' policies, it's a bit overwhelmin' for me. What's your take on it? I've been hearin' a lot about the importance of infrastructure from me mam, she's always goin' on about how it's the backbone of the country. But, anyway, enough about that serious stuff. What've ye been up to in yer free time? Seen any good shows or anythin'? Actually, I went to see a musical in London last weekend. It was brilliant! Have you ever seen Les Misérables? Aye, I saw it a few years ago! I loved it, the music's so powerful. I've been listenin' to the soundtrack nonstop since then. What did ye think of it, then? I thought it was amazing. The cast was incredible, and the set design was so impressive. I loved how they used the revolving stage to create the different scenes. And, of course, the music is just iconic. Definitely, like! I remember cryin' me eyes out during "I Dreamed a Dream". It's just so emotional, ye know? An' the story's so powerful, it really makes ye think about the struggles people faced back then. Exactly! It's a really important story, and it's amazing how the musical brings it to life. I've been listenin' to the soundtrack nonstop since I saw it, too.

Ah, lah, I'm made up with how this paint's goin' down, int I? Me back yard's gonna look like a right palace when we're finished. Aye, it's comin' on alright, Dave. You've got a good eye for colour, y'know. I was thinkin', have you seen them new plans for the urban development down by the docks? Yeah, I saw 'em in the Echo. I'm not sure what to make of 'em, to be honest. Part of me thinks it's great that they're investin' in the area, but another part of me's worried about all the character bein' ripped out. It's a shame, 'cause that's what makes Liverpool special, y'know? Anyway, enough about that. How's the lecturin' goin'? Still got a passion for it? Oh, definitely, Steve. I love seein' the students develop their understanding of literature. We've been studyin' some great stuff recently, like Shakespeare's comedies. Speakin' of which, have you seen any good films lately? I've been meanin' to get to the cinema, but I haven't had a chance. Actually, I took the missus to see that new Scorsese film last week. It was sound, but I think I nodded off for a bit – been workin' some long hours lately! You should give it a go, though. I reckon you'd appreciate it. By the way, how's your paintin' comin' along? I've been thinkin' about startin' a new project, maybe somethin' inspired by the city. I've been lookin' for some second-hand art supplies, actually – do you know anyone who's gettin' rid of any? Now that you mention it, I think me mate's got a load of old art gear he's lookin' to get shot of. I can give him a ring if you like. What kind of things are you after? Just the usual, really – canvases, brushes, that sort of thing. And maybe some frames, if he's got any. I've been thinkin' about settin' some goals for myself, too – gettin' more into me paintin', maybe even exhibitin' some pieces.

Oh, look, Rachel, the scenery is just breathtaking, isn't it? The Tatra Mountains are stunning. I'm so glad we decided to take this route from Białka Tatrzańska to Tarnow. I know, it's amazing. I've never seen anything like it. The way the mountains rise up from the ground, it's like nothing I've ever seen before. And the cost of this trip has been really reasonable so far, don't you think? Yes, I was a bit worried about the expenses, but it seems like we've managed to keep them under control. Although, I have to say, I'm a bit concerned about how much we're spending on food. I feel like we've been out of touch for a while. Yeah, I spoke to Sarah the other day, and she was saying that she's been doing some clearing out of her flat. I've been feeling really overwhelmed with all my possessions lately, and the idea of just getting rid of everything and travelling sounds really appealing. Although, I have to say, I'm not sure I could do it full-time. I like having a bit of stability in my life. Yeah, I know what you mean. But it's funny, we've met so many people on this trip who are doing just that - travelling full-time and living out of a campervan or backpack. There was that couple we met at the last campsite, and they were telling us about how they've been on the road for years.

Ey up, how much longer till we get to Preston? I'm dyin' for a cuppa and a browse around the shops. Ah, about 20 minutes, I'd say. We're making good time, considering the traffic. So, have you lot decided what you're going to do at the Hay festival this year? Oh, I don't know, love. I was thinkin' we could just wander around and see what catches our eye. I've 'eard the book talks are always good, though. What do you think, pet? Yeah, that sounds like a plan. I've been readin' this really good book, "The Hunger Games". Have you read it, Petra? Actually, I have! I loved it. The whole series is great. I've been meanin' to get the new one, but I haven't had a chance yet. How's your mum doin', by the way? I've been meanin' to ask. She had this one book, "The Secret Garden", and she'd always do the voices for the characters. It was so funny! Aw, that sounds lovely. I used to love bein' read to when I was a kid, too. My mum would read us all these Slovakian folk tales, and we'd sit around the fire, listenin' to her stories. You know, I was thinkin' the other day, it's been ages since we've all been on a proper family holiday together. We should start lookin' into that, maybe somewhere in the UK, like the Lake District or sommat. Ooh, that sounds like a great idea, Dad! Can we go to the Lake District? I've always wanted to go there. And maybe we can stop at some of the old shops in the towns we visit, like the ones in Ambleside. That sounds like a lovely idea, John. And we can make sure to avoid the train strikes, too. I've 'eard they're goin' to be a right nuisance this summer. Ah, don't even get me started on the train strikes! It's a right mess, if you ask me.

Ah, it's so lovely to see you both! I hope I'm not interrupting anything important. I was in the area and thought I'd surprise you with a visit. Not at all, Mum! We're delighted to see you. Come on in, come on in. Would you like a cup of tea? That would be lovely, dear. Thank you. And how's my grandson doing? I haven't seen you in ages, young man! How's school? I'm telling you, this new laptop is a beast. The specs on it are insane. I've been testing it out for a few hours now and it's been handling everything I throw at it. Yeah, I can see that. I've done some basic computer maintenance in the past, so I might be able to help you troubleshoot the issue. Yeah, that would be great, thanks. I feel like everyone's so obsessed with it. I know what you mean. I've been trying to cut back on my own social media use lately. It's just so tempting to mindlessly scroll through your feeds all day. Same here. I've been trying to focus more on my YouTube channel instead. I've been uploading videos on mixed martial arts and it's been getting a pretty good response. That's cool. I've been getting into retro technology lately. I'm so glad we decided to meet up here, this bistro is lovely. I've been walking past it for weeks, wondering when it would open. The decor is really nice, isn't it? Yeah, it's great. I feel like the people we surround ourselves with can really shape who we are and how we see ourselves. Hmm, that's a good question.

I'm so excited for the Dorset Steam Fair this weekend, Dad. I've been looking forward to it for weeks. Have you managed to get the tickets yet? Ah, yes, love. I got them online yesterday. I'm telling you, it was a nightmare trying to sail from Jeddah to Cyprus. I had no idea it was going to be so complicated. What happened, Margaret? I'm so glad we decided to grab lunch here, the Printing House has such a lovely atmosphere. I've always been fascinated by the history of Cambridge University Press. I'm so excited for Christmas this year, I've been playing this new internet game and I'm really getting into it. It's all about strategy and psychology, trying to outsmart the other players. Ah'm tellin' thee, it's been ages since we've all been out together. How's life been treatin' yer, then? It's been alright, I s'pose. Just been keepin' busy wi' college work and playin' me guitar. Alrigh' pet, 'ave you 'eard about this new bus route they're plannin' to introduce in Cambridge? I was readin' about it in the local paper this mornin'. Yeah, I saw somethin' about it online. I'm so glad we decided to meet up for lunch today, girls. It's been too long since we've had a chance to catch up. And this place is lovely, isn't it? The food is just delicious. Absolutely, Maeve. I'm so glad we decided to walk along the Thames today, it's such a lovely day out. And look, there's the O2 Arena, it's amazing how it's become such an iconic landmark, isn't it? I'm so glad we're all indoors today, this rain is relentless. I was supposed to go to the park with my niece and nephew, but I don't think that's happening now. Ey up, lah! I'm tellin' yer, I was at this meeting with a client from London the other day, and I couldn't help but notice how posh their accent was. Ah'm tellin' thee, t'birds are singing their 'earts out this mornin'! Must be forecastin' a grand day, don't you think, Margaret? Indeed, I do! Although, I must admit, I'm not as familiar with the different birdsongs as you are, Barbara. You're always teachin' me sommat new. What's that one that sounds like a laugh? Ah, that'll be t'green woodpecker! They've got a right distinctive call, haven't they? An' t'other day, I 'eard a blackcap in t'garden. Such a pretty song, so it is. By t'way, 'ave you sorted out that alarm clock of yours? You were sayin' it were keepin' you awake at night. Oh, yes! I finally got a new one, and it's been a game-changer. An' I've been meanin' to ask, 'ave you 'eard from our mutual friend, Susan? I 'aven't seen 'er in ages, an' I was wonderin' how she's doin'. Anyway, she said to say 'ello, an' she'll come visit soon. That's good to 'ear! I was gettin' a bit worried about 'er. An' speakin' of the dentist, I 'ad a right ordeal last time I went. 'Ad a nosebleed while they were workin' on my teeth, can you believe it? What a mess! Oh dear, that sounds awful! I'm sure it was just a one-off, though. I've 'ad a few nosebleeds myself, especially when the weather changes. But I've found that puttin' a bit of Vaseline up me nostrils 'elps to stop 'em. That's a good tip, thanks for sharin'! I'll 'ave to give it a go. Now, 'ave you started thinkin' about your gardenin' plans for this year? I was thinkin' of gettin' some new flowers in, maybe some more bird-friendly plants.

It's so lovely to catch up with you, Sarah. I feel like it's been ages since we last saw each other. How have you been? I've been good, thanks, Emma. Just been keeping busy with work and everything. You know how it is. But I have to say, I'm really excited to be here in Cambridge. I've always loved this city. How about you? What's new with you? Oh, you know, same old same old. Teaching keeps me on my toes, that's for sure. But I've been thinking about making a change, to be honest. I've been feeling a bit...restless, I suppose. I've been considering a career change, maybe something a bit more relaxed. Really? What did you have in mind? You've always been so passionate about teaching. I know, I know. And I do love it, but it's just so...exhausting. All the paperwork and bureaucracy...sometimes I feel like I'm not actually making a difference, you know? And I've been thinking about writing a book, too. I've always loved writing, and I think it could be a great way to express myself. That sounds amazing! You should totally go for it. What kind of book were you thinking of writing? Well, I'm not entirely sure yet. Maybe something about my experiences as a teacher? Or maybe something entirely different. I've always been fascinated by the way people use social media, and how it affects our relationships...maybe I could write about that. That's really interesting. I've been thinking about that a lot lately, too. It's like, on the one hand, social media can be this amazing tool for connecting with people and sharing ideas...but on the other hand, it can be so...toxic. And it's like, what's the point of it all, you know? Exactly! And it's not just the toxicity, it's the way people present these perfect, curated versions of themselves...it's like, nobody's life is really like that, is it? And it can be so damaging to people's self-esteem and mental health. Totally. And it's like, as a social worker, I see the effects of that all the time. People feeling lonely and isolated, despite being constantly connected...it's just so sad. Yeah...it's like, we need to find a way to use social media in a healthier way, you know?

I'm so glad I finally got to meet you in person, Mr... um, I'm so sorry, I've forgotten your name. Ah, please, call me Dave. We've met before, but only briefly. I'm glad you could drop by for a cuppa. Thank you, Dave. Your home is lovely. I especially love the garden. I've been meaning to get some gardening done myself, but I just haven't had the time. Ah, yes, gardening is a great hobby. I've been doing it for years. It's a good way to relax and get some exercise. I've been trying to get my grandson into it, but he's more interested in playing video games. Ah, yes, I know the feeling. That's wonderful! I'm a language teacher myself. I've been working at a local school for a few years now. It's challenging, but rewarding. I love seeing my students progress and become more confident in their language skills. Ah, that's great. I've always been interested in languages. I studied French and German at university. But I have to say, the education system can be quite frustrating at times. The bureaucracy and lack of funding can be really challenging. I know what you mean. It's been getting worse over the years. When I was teaching, we had more freedom to design our own curricula and tailor our teaching to our students' needs. Now, it seems like everything is dictated by standardized tests and government mandates. Exactly! And it's not just the education system. I've been noticing that there's been a lot of crime in the area lately. I've had a few students who have been affected by it, and it's really concerning. Yes, it's a shame.

Ah'm tellin' thee, that curry we had last night were reight good! Ah'm still thinkin' about it now. Aye, it were canny! Ah loved the flavors they used. Did ye try the naan bread? It were freshly made, an' it were lovely. Ah did, an' it were perfect for dippin' in the sauce. Ah'm a big fan o' Indian food, me. Oh, just the usual stuff – some indie, some rock, maybe a bit o' pop. We can make a playlist an' get everyone to contribute some songs. That sounds like a great idea! Ah love makin' playlists. Can we include some Northern bands, like Arctic Monkeys or The Kaiser Chiefs? Definitely! I'm a big fan o' the Arctic Monkeys. An' we should also include some German music, just for a bit o' variety. Maybe some Kraftwerk or Rammstein? Rammstein, eh? They're a bit too heavy for me taste, but ah suppose it'll be a good laugh. What about films, then? Has anyone seen any good ones recently? Ah just saw the new Bond film, an' it were really good. The action scenes were incredible. Ah've 'eard it's good, but ah'm not a big fan o' Bond films. Ah prefer rom-coms, meself. Has anyone seen any good ones o' those recently? Actually, ah saw "Crazy Rich Asians" recently, an' it were really enjoyable. The humor were great, an' the story were interesting. Ah've 'eard o' that one, but ah 'aven't seen it yet. Ah'll 'ave to give it a go, then. Maybe we can 'ave a film night an' watch it together? Sounds like a plan, mate!

I'm telling you, the new gym in town is a game-changer. I've been going there for a few weeks now and I can already see the difference. They have top-notch equipment and the staff is really friendly. Oh, yeah? I've been thinking of joining a gym myself. What's the membership like? Is it expensive? It's actually pretty reasonable. I'm paying about £30 a month, which is a steal considering what you get. Plus, they have a really good selection of classes, from yoga to spin classes. I've been meaning to get back into exercise myself. I used to love going to the gym, but since I started working as an editor, I just haven't had the time. We're thinking of going to Glastonbury. Have you guys been before? Yeah, I went a few years ago. It was amazing. The atmosphere is just electric. But, man, the queues for the toilets are something else. Yeah, I've heard the queues can be pretty bad.

Ah'm tellin' ye, that referee's made a right mess of it! How could he no' see that was a foul? I know, I was shoutin' at the telly too. But you've got to admit, it's been a pretty excitin' match so far. I'm on the edge of me seat. Aye, it has! Newcastle's doin' all right, considerin' they're playin' against Manchester City. I'm just hope they can keep it up and get a result. Fingers crossed, eh? So, have you given any more thought to what we're gonna do over Easter? My sister's invited us to her place in Oxford, but I was thinkin' maybe we could just have a quiet weekend here in Cambridge instead? Hmm, that's a tough one. I do love spendin' time with your sister and her family, but at the same time, it would be nice to just chill out here and not have to worry about travellin' anywhere. What do you think about watchin' some films over Easter? We could have a marathon or sommat. Sounds like a great idea to me! I've been meanin' to catch up on some of the new releases. What kind of films were you thinkin' of watchin'? Any particular genre? Well, I've been in the mood for some action films lately. Maybe we could watch some of the Marvel movies or sommat? I've also been wantin' to see that new Bond film that just came out. Brilliant choice! I've been wantin' to see the new Bond film too. And we could always watch some of the classics, like the old James Bond films or some of the Star Wars movies. I'm game for whatever, really. Ooh, that sounds like a great plan! And we can't forget about the football over Easter, either. There's usually some big matches on, isn't there? Ah, you're right! The Easter weekend's always a big one for football fans. We'll have to make sure we've got all the fixtures written down so we don't miss any of the important ones. You can bet I've already got the whole schedule printed out and stuck on the fridge. I've even got a little sweepstake goin' on with me mates from work to see who can predict the most results correctly. You're such a competitive one, aren't you?

Ah, would ye look at that little fella, he's the spit of his father when he was a young lad. I'm tellin' ye, it's like lookin' at an old photo of myself. Grandda, you're so silly. That's me when I was little, isn't it, Mum? Yes, sweetie, that's you on your fourth birthday. You had just learned how to ride a bike and were so proud of yourself. And I remember that day like it was yesterday. We had a big party for ye in the back garden, and ye got a brand new bike with streamers on the handlebars. Ye were the happiest young fella I'd ever seen. Oh, I couldn't help but overhear ye talkin' about birthdays. I've got a great story about my own birthday when I was a wee lass. We used to go to the fun fair in Glasgow, and I always looked forward to it for weeks. Fun fair? That sounds like so much fun! Do they have fun fairs in Ireland, Grandda? Ah, yes, we do! In fact, there's a great one that comes to Cork every summer. We should take ye and yer mum this year, what do ye think? That would be lovely, wouldn't it, sweetie? We can make a whole day of it. And speakin' of lovelies, have ye seen the pictures of my grandson runnin' the London marathon? He did a fantastic job, finished in under four hours. Under four hours, that's no small feat! I'm sure he must have been trainin' for months. Did he enjoy it, or was it just a chore for him? Oh, he loved every minute of it! He's already plannin' to do it again next year. And he's also been talkin' about goin' to Iceland for a holiday. Have ye ever been, son? Actually, I've been thinkin' about takin' the family to Iceland for a trip. I've heard the landscapes are just breathtaking. And maybe we can even catch a movie at the cinema in Reykjavik, I've heard it's a unique experience. Yeah! Can we go to the cinema, Grandda? I want to see the new superhero movie. We'll see, sweetie. But first, let's finish lookin' at these photos and reminisce about old times. Ah, now this one's a great picture.

I'm so glad we're having this dinner together, it's been too long. I've been meaning to try out this new recipe for chicken parmesan, and I'm excited to hear what you think of it. It smells amazing in here, I'm sure it will be delicious. You've always been a great cook, ever since we were at university together. Remember those dodgy pizza nights we used to have in our flat? Oh, how could I forget? We used to put so many toppings on those pizzas, they would practically collapse under the weight. And don't even get me started on the state of our kitchen afterwards. You young people and your fancy food. In my day, we were lucky to have a hot meal on the table, let alone all these fancy toppings and sauces. Oh, Mum, you're such a card. We're not that young anymore, you know. But yes, food has certainly changed over the years, hasn't it? I mean, have you seen the size of the vocabulary we use to describe food now? It's like a whole different language. That's so true. I was reading a book the other day, and the author was describing a character's favorite dish, and they used the word "umami". I had to look it up, I had no idea what it meant. Umami? What's wrong with just saying it tastes nice? All these fancy words, just to describe something that's going to end up in your belly anyway. Well, Mum, you have to admit, words can be powerful. They can evoke emotions and memories, and that's especially true when it comes to food. Think about it, just the mention of certain smells or tastes can transport us back to our childhood. Exactly. Like the smell of freshly baked cookies, or the taste of homemade soup. It's like our brains are hardwired to associate certain foods with certain memories or emotions. Oh, yes. My mother used to make the most wonderful soup when I was a child. It was a big pot of vegetables and scraps of meat, but it was the most comforting thing in the world. And the smell of it cooking on the stove... Mum, what are you thinking about? Oh, just my childhood, I suppose. Playing with my siblings, and our old toys.

Blimey, I'm gettin' a bit peckish, ain't you, love? These sandwiches you made are lovely, by the way. Oh, thank you, dear. I'm glad you're enjoyin' 'em. I was thinkin' we could have a nice cup of tea to go with 'em. I've got a fresh pot just waitin' to be poured. That sounds like just the ticket. I've been thinkin' a lot about me childhood lately, and it's amazin' how a nice cuppa can bring back all sorts of memories. Oh, really? What kind of memories have you been thinkin' about? You know I love hearin' about your childhood in Norfolk. Well, I was thinkin' about me old mate, Davey. We used to get into all sorts of trouble together, whether it was explorin' the woods or playin' pranks on the local shopkeeper. Good times, they were. You've told me so many stories about Davey. I feel like I know him myself. What happened to him, again? Did he stay in Norfolk or move away? Ah, Davey... well, he ended up movin' to London, didn't he? Got a job as a mechanic or somethin', and I lost touch with him for a while. But we reconnected a few years ago, and it was like no time had passed at all. We still keep in touch, exchange Christmas cards and whatnot. That's lovely. It's always nice to have friends from childhood that you can stay in touch with. I've got a few old friends from Harrow that I still keep in touch with, too. We don't see each other as often as we'd like, but we always have a good natter when we do. Yeah, it's important to hold onto those relationships, ain't it? I mean, people come and go in your life, but the ones from your childhood... they're special. They knew you when you were just a young whippersnapper, before you got all old and crotchety like me. Oh, don't be ridiculous, you're not old and crotchety! You're just... seasoned, that's all. Besides, I think you're still as much of a whippersnapper as you ever were. Oh, thanks, love. I think you're just tryin' to flatter me, but I'll take it anyway. You know, speakin' of childhood, I was thinkin' about me old school days the other day...

I'm tellin' you, I had the most interestin' conversation with one of me students the other day about the English language. This little lad, must've been about 9 years old, asked me why we have so many exceptions to the rules in English. I mean, I've never really thought about it, but it's true, innit? We've got words that sound the same but are spelt different, like "to", "too", and "two". Oh, that's so cool! I love it when kids ask questions like that. It's like, they're just startin' to figure out how language works, and it's all so fascinatin' to them. I've had similar conversations with me own students, but more about why we use certain words in certain contexts. Like, why we use "get" instead of "receive" in informal situations. Yeah, and it's not just the kids, is it? I mean, I've been workin' on this copywritin' project, and I've been thinkin' about how language is used in different ways dependin' on the audience. Like, if I'm writin' for a young audience, I'll use more colloquial language, but if I'm writin' for a business audience, I'll use more formal language. Exactly! And it's funny you should mention that, 'cause I was just talkin' to our mate, Emily, the other day, and she was tellin' me about how she's been strugglin' to find the right tone for her blog. She wants to be friendly and approachable, but also professional, you know? Oh, yeah! I know what you mean. I've been tryin' to help her out with that, actually. We were brainstormin' ideas for her blog, and I suggested she try usin' more conversational language, like we're usin' now. You know, just relaxin' into it and bein' herself. Ooh, that's a great idea! And speakin' of great ideas, has everyone got their presents for Sarah's birthday yet? I still need to get hers, and I was thinkin' of gettin' her that new book by her favourite author. Ah, yeah! I got her a lovely scarf, actually. And I was thinkin' we could all go out for dinner to celebrate? Maybe that new restaurant that just opened up near here? Sounds like a plan to me! But first, I need to deal with me car problems. It's been actin' up somethin' awful, and I don't know what's wrong with it.

Yer know, I've been livin' in this neighbourhood fer years now, an' I gotta say, it's changed a lot. There's a lot more new faces around, an' I'm not sure if that's a good thing or not. What do yer think, lah? Ah, I know what yer mean! I've lived 'ere me whole life, an' it's like a different place now. I mean, I'm not against progress an' all that, but sometimes I feel like we're losin' the soul of the place. An' have yer seen the state of the streets lately? Me wife is still workin' hard as a teacher, an' the kids are keepin' us on our toes as usual. Me eldest is gettin' into Harry Potter at the moment, an' it's like he's obsessed or somethin'! Which one's yer favourite, Mr... sorry, I don't know yer name, sir! Ah, it's John, lad! An' I'm glad yer a fan of Harry Potter, too! I think me favourite's probably "The Prisoner of Azkaban", but I'm not sure, I love 'em all, really! What about you, which one's yer favourite? Anyway, back to the neighbourhood... I was talkin' to me mate the other day, an' she was tellin' me about all the troubles they've been havin' with them ISIS lot. I don't know what the world's comin' to, honestly. It's like they're tryin' to destroy everythin' that's good an' decent. Oh, don't even get me started on that! It's terrifying, really. I mean, I know we're supposed to be tolerant an' all that, but sometimes I think we're bein' too soft on them.

I'm telling you, Nepal is a place I've always wanted to visit. The culture, the scenery, it's just so fascinating. Have you given any more thought to joining me on this trip, Margaret? And speaking of school, how's your job as school display co-ordinator going, Barbara?

Ah'm tellin' thee, it's been a right mad week at work. We've had conferences comin' out of our ears, and ah've been runnin' around like a headless chicken tryin' to keep everything organized. You should totally come work with me! We could do with someone with your organizational skills. But seriously, Rebecca, what makes thee want to leave thy current job? Is it the work itself, or the company? Ah think it's a bit of both, to be honest. Ah love the work, but the company can be a bit...much, sometimes. Ah'm not sure if ah'm just bein' paranoid, but ah feel like ah'm not bein' utilized to me full potential, if thou knows what ah mean. Yeah, ah do know what thou mean. Ah've felt like that before too. But sometimes, thou just have to take a leap of faith and try sommat new. Ah mean, what's the worst that could happen, right?

I'm telling you, it's a absolute disaster. They can't just demolish our local library like that. It's a vital part of the community. What's the point of having a borough council if they're not going to listen to what the people want? I know, I've been thinking about that a lot lately. We should start a petition to save it. I've got some experience with that sort of thing from my admin job, so I could help with the logistics. What do you think? That's a fantastic idea! I was thinking of talking to some of the other regulars at the library, see if we can get some support. And we should definitely get the local paper involved, get some press coverage. Do you think we could get a thousand signatures? Easily, I think. And if we time it right, we could present it to the council at the next meeting. I've got a friend who works in the council office, I could get some inside info on the best way to go about it. You know, it's funny, I was just talking to him the other day about the new shifts they're implementing at the office. Apparently, they're going to be working some crazy hours. Ugh, don't even get me started on that. I've been having to deal with some crazy shifts at the transcription office too. It's like they think we're robots or something. And it's not just the hours, it's the workload too. I'm constantly stressed out. You know what they say, "use it or lose it". I've been trying to do some brain training exercises in my free time, just to keep my mind sharp. Ah, yeah! I've been doing some of those too. I found this great app that gives you puzzles and games to do. It's actually really fun. And I've been using mnemonics to help me remember things. You know, like "Richard Of York Gave Battle In Vain" to remember the colours of the rainbow? Oh, yeah! I used to use that one all the time when I was at university. It's amazing how well it works. But, anyway, back to the library. Do you think we could get some of the local businesses on board? Maybe they could donate some money or resources to help with the petition?

I'm tellin' ya, those Jehovah's Witnesses are a persistent lot, ain't they? Came to me door last week, tryin' to convert me to their way of thinkin'. I politely listened, but I told 'em I'm a man of science, not faith. Ah, yes! I've had me share of 'em too, mate. They're like a bad cold, keep comin' back even when you think you've gotten rid of 'em. My wife, God rest her soul, she used to love talkin' to 'em, though. I'm so glad we decided to order pizza tonight, I'm starving after that long day of lectures. Definitely, me too. I've been thinking about this all day. Alright, who got the most toppings on their slice? I think that would be me, I got extra olives and mushrooms. Ugh, olives are disgusting. How can you eat them? Oh, come on, they're not that bad. Maybe we could start by playing some geography-based games to get us in the mood? Oh, we should play Articulate or Heads Up, those are always so much fun. And after that, we can watch a movie, I've been wanting to see Cloud Atlas again. I'm more in the mood for something lighter, how about we watch Twilight and make fun of it? That sounds like a great idea. And we can quote some Jack Whitehall jokes to make it even more entertaining. You know what would be even better? Watching The Big Fat Quiz and trying to answer the questions before the contestants do. Yes, that's a great idea. And after that, we can discuss the Chaos Walking trilogy, I just finished reading it. Oh, how was it? I've been meaning to start reading it. You should, it's really good. And speaking of good TV shows, has everyone seen The Vampire Diaries? Yes, I love it. And I'm also hooked on How I Met Your Mother, it's so funny. You know what's not funny? Our mutual friend's sense of humor, have you seen his tweets?

Alrigh' then, how's work been treatin' ye? I feel like I haven't seen ye all week, and we're already halfway through it. Ah, it's been keepin' me busy, as per usual. We've got a few big projects comin' up, so I've been puttin' in some long hours. But, you know, it's all worth it in the end. How about you? How's life as a Corpus Administrator treatin' you? It's been alright, like. I've been gettin' used to the new software we got in, so that's been a bit of a challenge. But, I mean, it's not like I'm savin' lives or anythin', so I shouldn't complain. I did have a funny incident the other day, though. I was workin' on this one project, and I found this really old text from, like, the 1800s or sommat. And, I swear, the language they used back then is like a different world. That sounds amazin'! I can imagine. I mean, I've seen some old documents in my line of work, but nothin' that old. What was the text about, if you don't mind me askin'? It was just a load of letters from this one bloke to his mate. Nothin' too interestin', but the way they wrote was just...different. They used all these fancy words and phrases that you just don't hear anymore. I had to look up half of 'em just to understand what they were on about. And the spellin'! Oh my god, it was like they made up their own rules. I can imagine. I've seen some old technical documents that are like that. It's like they're written in a different language. But, hey, at least you're learnin' sommat new, right? You're gettin' to see how language has evolved over time. Exactly! And it's not just the language itself, it's the way people thought and expressed themselves back then. It's like gettin' a glimpse into a different world. I mean, I've always been interested in history, but this is like...I don't know, it's just a different level of understanding, I s'pose. That's really cool. I've always been more of a numbers person myself, but I can appreciate the value of learnin' about language and history. Maybe one day you can teach me some of these old words and phrases, and I can impress my mates with me knowledge of antiquated language.

I'm tellin' ya, the weather's been dreadful lately. All this rain's been playin' havoc with me joints. I can barely move me knees in the mornin' without a spot of trouble. Oh, don't even get me started, love. I've been havin' the same problem. Me arthritis has been actin' up somethin' fierce. I've had to take extra pills just to get through the day. I'm so sorry to hear that, Uncle. Maybe we should get you to see the doctor again? Get them to take a look at your medication and see if there's anything else they can do to help. Ah, don't fuss, dear. I've been to the doctor's enough times already. They just tell me the same thing: "Keep takin' the pills and try to stay warm." Like it's that easy. That's not very helpful, is it? I mean, surely there must be some other options available? Have you considered lookin' into alternative therapies? I've heard acupuncture can be quite effective for joint pain. Ooh, that's a good idea, actually. I've got a friend who swears by it. She goes to this lovely lady in the village who does all sorts of holistic treatments. Well, I suppose it's worth a shot. Can't hurt to try, eh? But anyway, enough about me creaky joints. How 'bout the weather, then? When's the sun supposed to come out again? According to the forecast, we're supposed to get a bit of a break next week. Fingers crossed, eh? Yeah, I could do with a bit of sunshine. I've been stuck inside markin' papers all week and I'm startin' to feel like a hermit. Well, you're welcome to come out into the garden with me anytime. I could do with some company while I'm doin' me gardenin'. Oh, speakin' of which, did anyone see the football match last night? Norwich City's been doin' all right lately, haven't they? Yeah, I caught the highlights this mornin'. They played a crackin' game. I reckon they've got a good chance of gettin' promoted this season. Oh, you're such a optimist, Alex. But I suppose it's nice to have a bit of hope, especially with the way the weather's been. You know, I was thinkin' of gettin' a new tablet.

I'm so glad we're all finally catching up together. It feels like it's been ages since we've had a chance to talk. I know, I've missed you girls so much. How was your week, Emily? How's work going? It's been okay, just busy with the usual administrative tasks. But I did hear some exciting news - my cousin is getting married next summer! Oh, that's amazing! I love weddings. Who's the lucky guy? His name is Alex, and they met through mutual friends. They're really cute together. Aw, that's so sweet. I'm sure the wedding will be beautiful. Are you going to be a bridesmaid? Yeah, I am! I'm really excited, but also a bit nervous. I've never been a bridesmaid before. Don't worry, you'll be great. We'll all be there to support you. Speaking of which, have you guys heard from Sarah lately? I feel like we haven't caught up with her in ages. Yeah, I talked to her last week. She's doing well, just busy with work and stuff. She said she might come over for dinner next weekend, though. That sounds like fun. We should definitely plan something. Maybe we can even get the boys to come over and make it a big dinner party. Sounds like a plan to me. I'll talk to my boyfriend and see if he can come. How about you, Emily, are you seeing anyone special at the moment? Actually, I am. His name is Jack, and we've been dating for a few months now. He's really nice, and I think you guys will like him. Aw, that's great! We'll have to meet him soon. Do you think he's the marrying type? I don't know, we'll see. I'm not thinking about marriage just yet, but it's definitely something I'd like to have in the future. Yeah, me too. I think we're all at that age where we're starting to think about settling down and having kids. Definitely. But for now, let's just enjoy our freedom and have fun. Who's up for going out for dinner next weekend? I am! Where did you have in mind? There's a new restaurant that just opened up downtown. I've heard great things about it.

I'm tellin' ya, I don't know how you young folks keep up with all this new-fangled technology. I mean, I've got me mobile phone, but I only use it for rangin' me mates and playin' a bit of Sudoku. Oh, come on, Brian! You're not that old! You can learn to use a computer and get on the internet. It's not that hard, I assure you. I don't know, love. I've never been one for book learnin', and all that technical stuff just goes right over me 'ead. Me brother's kid is always tryin' to teach me, but I just can't seem to get the hang of it. Ah, I think I can relate, Brian. I've got some students in me class who are absolute whizzes with technology, but others who struggle to even turn on a computer. It's all about how you're taught, I think. That's true. I've been tryin' to get me own grandson to teach me how to use this Facebook thingy, but he just laughs and says I'm too old for it. Ah, kids these days, eh? Think they know it all just because they've got a fancy phone and a computer. In me day, we didn't need all that to have fun. We just played outside with our mates and used our imaginations. I think that's one of the things that's missing from modern childhood, actually. Kids these days are so glued to their screens, they're missin' out on all the fresh air and exercise they need. I've been tryin' to get me own students to put down their phones and go outside during break times, but it's an uphill battle, I tell ya. Oh, I completely agree. I used to love takin' the kids I childminded for on outings to the park or the woods. They'd run around and play for hours, and it was great to see 'em gettin' some exercise and havin' fun. Speakin' of which, have you heard from me niece lately? She's the one who's always goin' on about her horses. I swear, that girl's got a passion for 'em that's just infectious. Ah, yes! I've met your niece a few times, Brian. She's a lovely girl, and she's always talkin' about her horses.

I'm so glad we finally have a chance to catch up, John. It feels like it's been ages since we last spoke. How have you been? Ah, I've been all right, thanks for asking, Sarah. Just keeping busy with the garden and whatnot. Can't complain. Although, I did just get back from a lovely trip to the coast with the family. The grandchildren loved it, and it was great to spend some quality time with them. Oh, that sounds wonderful! I'm sure they had a blast. I've been meaning to take my own students on a trip to the coast to practice their English skills in a more immersive environment. Do you think that would be a good idea? Absolutely, I think it's a cracking idea! The kids would love it, and it's always beneficial to get them out of the classroom and into the real world, isn't it? I remember when I was in charge of the company, we used to take the employees on team-building trips to the countryside, and it always brought everyone together. Exactly! And it's not just about the language skills, either. It's about broadening their horizons and introducing them to different cultures and ways of life. Speaking of which, have you ever thought about learning a new language yourself? I've been thinking of starting a language exchange program for adults in the community. Actually, I've always been fascinated by languages, but I never had the chance to learn one when I was younger. I did try to learn some French when I was on holiday in France a few years ago, but it didn't quite stick. Maybe I'll have to take you up on that offer and join your language exchange program. That would be brilliant! I think you'd really enjoy it. And who knows, maybe you can even teach me some of your gardening skills in exchange. I've been trying to get my own garden started, but I'm not having much luck. Ha! I'd be happy to help you out with that. Gardening is all about trial and error, you know. And I've had my fair share of mistakes over the years. But it's a great hobby, and it keeps me active and engaged. I can imagine. I've been meaning to ask, what do you like to do in your free time, apart from gardening?

Blud, I'm so done with this week, innit? Valentine's Day was a right mess for me. My boyfriend forgot to get me a present, can you believe it? Oh, that's rubbish! What did you do, give him a row or what? Course I did! I was like, "How could you forget, it's Valentine's Day, ain't it?" And he's all like, "I'm sorry, babe, I was busy with work." Busy with work, my foot! He was probably busy playin' FIFA with his mates. That's so typical, though! Men, eh? My cousin's boyfriend did the same thing, and she was fumin'! They were supposed to go to the cinema, but he cancelled last minute. Ugh, don't even get me started on the cinema! We were supposed to watch that new rom-com, but it was sold out. We ended up watchin' some action movie instead, and I was so bored out of my mind. Aw, that's a shame. I love a good rom-com, me. We should go watch one this weekend, just us girls. We can make a day of it, go shopping, get some food... Ooh, that sounds like a plan, babes! I'm so down for that. But, first, we need to decide where to eat. I'm so sick of the food here at the uni canteen. It's all just the same old rubbish every day. Totally! I know this one restaurant in town that does the best chicken parmesan. We should try that out. And after, we can hit the shops, get some retail therapy. Yaaas, sounds like a wicked plan! But, you know what's been gettin' on my nerves lately? People always ask me to repeat myself 'cause they can't understand my accent. Like, hello, I'm from London, innit? My accent's not that bad! Ah, I feel you, girl! People always do that to me too, 'cause of my Midlands twang. But, you know, I think it's quite funny when they try to mimic our accents. Like, this one time, I was talkin' to this bloke from the South, and he was tryin' to do my accent, but it sounded more like a mix of everything! Oh, that's hilarious! I had this one lecturer, right, and she was from, like, the North or somethin', and she had this really thick accent.

I'm telling you, it's unbelievable the way they're handling the racism issue in the States. I mean, it's like they're not even trying to make a change. I know, right? It's infuriating. And it's not just the States, either. We've got our own problems with racism here in the UK. Have you seen the latest stats on stop and search? Yeah, I saw something about it online. It's disgusting. I don't understand why they can't just admit that there's a problem and work to fix it. Oh, sorry, can I get the soy sauce, please? Here you go. And I totally agree with you. It's like they're just trying to sweep it under the rug and hope nobody notices. Anyway, how's your ramen? I got the spicy miso, it's really good. Mmm, mine's really good too. I got the tonkotsu. So, how's work been? Any interesting stories you're working on? Actually, yeah. I've been investigating some stuff about gentrification in East London. It's crazy what's going on. These big corporations are just buying up all the properties and pricing out the locals. It's like they don't even care about the community. That's awful. I've seen it happening in some of the areas I've worked in, too. It's all about the money, isn't it? They don't care who they're pushing out as long as they can make a profit. And it's not just the housing, either. I've seen it in my own industry, with these big architecture firms coming in and pricing out the smaller practices. Exactly! It's like, what's the point of having all these fancy new developments if the people who actually live in the area can't afford to stay? And it's all tied up in this whole capitalist system, you know? It's like, the more money you have, the more power you have, and the more you can just steamroll over everyone else. Absolutely. I mean, I'm not saying I have all the answers or anything, but it seems like we need to find a way to make the system more equitable. Maybe some kind of...I don't know, rent control or something? Yeah, that's not a bad idea.

I'm tellin' ya, I'm goin' to miss her so much when she starts nursery. It's hard to believe she's already at that age. I know, Mum, it feels like just yesterday we were bringin' her home from the hospital. But she'll be fine, and it'll be good for her to socialise with other kids. I know that, love. It's just...I've gotten so used to havin' her around all the time. I'm goin' to have to get used to bein' back at work and not bein' able to see her during the day. You'll be okay, Mum. You've been preparein' for this for months. And think of all the things you can do with your free time now. We can start plannin' some holidays, just the two of us, or maybe even a family trip to the seaside. That sounds lovely, actually. I've been thinkin' about takin' her to the Lake District. She loves bein' outdoors, and it's such a beautiful place. That's a great idea! She'd love it there. And we can start lookin' into weenin' her off the bottle soon, too. The doctor said it's a good time to start introducin' some solid foods. Yeah, I've been meanin' to start doin' that, but it's just been so easy to keep givin' her the bottle. I know it's not the best habit, though. Don't worry, Mum, we'll figure it out together. And I've been meanin' to ask, have you seen that new show on TV, the one with the detective who solves all the crimes? Oh, you mean the one with the handsome lead actor? Yes, I have seen it, and I'm hooked! I love a good mystery. Yeah, me too! I've been watchin' it with my friends at uni, and we're all obsessed. We should have a watch party when you're back at work, and I can come over and keep you company. That sounds like a great idea, love. I'd love to have some company during the day. And speakin' of work, I'm a bit nervous about goin' back. I've been out of the workforce for so long, I'm not sure I remember how to do anything! Don't be daft, Mum! You'll be fine. You're smart and capable, and you'll pick it up in no time.

I'm telling you, it's been a chaotic day. I had to deal with a difficult customer at work and then I had to rush to the police station to give a statement about the incident that happened last week. Ah, sorry to hear that, love. How did it go at the police station? Was it straightforward? Yeah, it was fine, I suppose. Just a lot of paperwork and questions. But I'm just glad it's over and done with. I don't think I'll have to go back again. Ugh, that sounds stressful. I had a pretty awful day too. We had a problem with one of the tills at the store and I had to sort it out. And to make matters worse, I got a call from EE about our phone bill. Apparently, we've gone over our data limit... again. Yeah, that's probably my fault. I've been streaming a lot of videos on my phone lately. I thought it might be something like that! Anyway, I've sorted it out with EE, but we need to be more careful with our data usage in the future. Definitely. We don't want to be paying over the odds for our phone bill every month. So, what are everyone's plans for the week? Well, I've got a meeting at work on Wednesday and then I'm free for the rest of the week. How about you, dear? I've got a fundraising event on Thursday evening, so I'll be busy with that. But I'm free on Friday and over the weekend. We should do something as a family. That sounds like a great idea. What did you have in mind? I don't know... maybe we could go for a walk in the countryside or visit a nearby attraction. What do you think? Yeah, that sounds good to me. As long as it's not too strenuous, I'm in. Don't worry, we won't make you climb any mountains. But seriously, it would be nice to spend some quality time together as a family. We've all been so busy lately. Absolutely. I'll check my schedule at work and make sure I can get the day off on Friday. And we can start looking into things to do around here. Brilliant. I'll make a few phone calls and see what I can come up with.

I'm telling you, mate, I've been binge-watching this TV show about Roman history and it's absolutely fascinating. The way they portray the struggles of the gladiators, it's like you're right there in the Colosseum. You and your Roman history obsession! I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen Spartacus? I heard it's a great show. Ah, yeah! I've seen it. It's brilliant. The way they depict the rebellion, it's so intense. And the characters, oh man... Spartacus himself, Crixus, Gannicus... they're all so well-developed. I know, right? I was really into it until... well, you know, the main character dies. I don't want to spoil it for you, but it's just so unexpected. Don't worry, mate, I've already seen it. And yeah, it's a real shame. I mean, the guy was only 33 when he died, right? It's just crazy to think about how short life can be. Exactly! It's like, we're just sitting here, enjoying our lives, and then suddenly... it's over. Like that musician, you know, the one who died of a malaria-related illness? Ah, you mean... I don't know, mate, I'm blanking on the name. But anyway, let's not get too morbid. What's new with you? How's the gardening business been treating you? It's been good, mate. Been keeping busy. I just got back from a trip to Cyprus, actually. My family's from there, you know. No, I didn't! What was it like? I've always wanted to visit. It's amazing. The food, the culture... everything's just so rich and vibrant. And the tea! Oh man, you have to try this Cypriot tea I brought back. It's like nothing you've ever tasted before. Really? I love trying new teas! And speaking of food, I've been experimenting with this mortar and pestle I got. I've been making all sorts of herbs and spices, grinding my own nuts... it's been a real game-changer for my cooking. You and your cooking, mate! I'm more of a simple guy, I just stick to what I know. But hey, if you're making some delicious chickpea bread or something, I'm happy to be your taste-tester. Deal! And actually, I was thinking of making some bread today.

I'm so glad it's the weekend, I was absolutely knackered after that English test on Friday. How did you find it, then? Ugh, don't even get me started! I thought it was going to be a breeze, but that comprehension passage was a right nightmare. I'm pretty sure I messed up the essay question, too. How about you, did you manage to finish on time? Yeah, I just about did. I was a bit worried I'd run out of time, but I managed to scribble down something for the last question. I'm not exactly thrilled about our chances of getting good grades, though. Mr. Johnson's been going on and on about how tough the marking is this year. Tell me about it! I swear, he loves making us suffer. Anyway, enough about that. Have you seen the sign-up sheet for the school orchestra? I was thinking of joining, and it would be more fun if you were in it too. Actually, I was thinking of joining as well! I actually really enjoy playing the flute, and it would be a great way to meet new people who like music. When's the audition, do you know? I think it's next Wednesday after school. We should totally practice together beforehand, make sure we're both ready. Oh, and speaking of school, have you seen the new artwork up in the hallway? It's from Miss Thompson's art class, and it's really impressive. Yeah, I saw it yesterday! That one painting of the landscape is incredible – I wish I could paint like that. Do you think we'll get to do anything like that in our art lessons this term? Hopefully! I heard Miss Thompson say something about us doing a project on watercolors soon. I'm not exactly the next Picasso, but it's always fun trying. By the way, have you started on that French homework that's due soon? Ugh, no... I've been putting it off, to be honest. I'm really struggling with the verb conjugations. Do you think Madame Dupont would be willing to give us some extra help if we asked? Probably, she's always saying that her door is open if we need anything. We should go see her together during lunch or something. Oh, and I almost forgot – have you heard about Alex and Sarah's fight in the cafeteria yesterday?

Ah'm tellin' thee, it's grand to see yer again, pet! How's life treatin' yer at school? It's alrigh', miss. Just tryin' to get through me exams, y'know? Aye, I do know! I've been there mesen, many years ago. So, what's on yer mind? Is it the maths or the science that's got yer stressed? It's a bit of both, really. But, I've been thinkin' about me options after school, an' I'm not sure what to do. Well, we can 'ave a chat about that, lad. What are yer interests? Are yer thinkin' about university or gettin' a job straight away? Ah, hello, dear! Sorry to interrupt, but I couldn't help but overhear. I'm Penny, a friend of... Ah, Penny, love! This is me young friend from Newcastle. We were just discussin' 'is options after school. Ah, lovely! I used to be a teacher, you know. What subjects are you enjoying, young man? I like history and geography, miss. Excellent choices! There are so many career paths you can take with those subjects. Have you thought about travelin' at all? It can be a great way to broaden yer horizons and learn about different cultures. That's a great point, Penny! I've always wanted to travel more mesen, but never had the chance. Maybe one day, eh? Yeah, I'd love to travel! But, me mam says it's too expensive. Ah, I know what she means, pet. Money's tight for a lot of people these days. But, there are ways to travel on a budget, y'know? Maybe we can look into that together, eh? And while we're on the subject of money, have you heard about the new affordable housing schemes they're introducin' in Darlington? It's supposed to help young people like you get on the property ladder. Really? That sounds interestin'! I'll have to look into it, thanks! Aye, it's always good to stay informed about what's goin' on in yer community, lad. Now, shall we get some refreshments? I'm buyin'! Oh, thank you, dear! I'll just have a cup of tea, please. Can I get a hot chocolate, miss? Course yer can, pet! I'll go order them now. So, young man, what do you think about the accent differences between Newcastle and Darlington? Do you think they're very distinct?

I'm telling you, it's getting more and more difficult to drive in Norwich. The traffic is terrible, and it's all because of the new roadworks on the A11. I was stuck in traffic for over an hour yesterday, trying to get to the university. Ah, come on, love. It's not that bad. I've been driving in London for years, and that's a whole different story. You think Norwich is bad? Try driving in the city during rush hour. Oh, I don't know how you two do it. I haven't driven in years, and I don't miss it one bit. Although, I did hear that they're trying to get people to walk and cycle more to combat obesity. Have you seen the statistics on obesity in this country? It's shocking. Yes, it's a real concern. As a lecturer, I see it in my students all the time. They're always eating junk food and sitting around playing video games. It's no wonder they're putting on weight. But, you know, it's not just about personal choice. There are genetic factors at play as well. That's true. I've been reading about the genetic links to obesity, and it's fascinating. Some people are just more prone to putting on weight, no matter how healthy they eat or how much exercise they get. Well, I think it's a bit of both, isn't it? Genes and environment, I mean. My mate Dave, he's always been a big bloke, but since he started going to the gym, he's lost a stone. It just shows that with a bit of effort, you can overcome your genetic predispositions. I suppose you're right. Although, I do think that some people are just more disposed to certain things. Like, I've always been allergic to nuts, and my mother was too. It must be genetic, don't you think? Absolutely. Allergies are a great example of how genes can play a role in our health. And speaking of health, have you heard about the new surgical operation they're doing for allergies? It's supposed to be revolutionary. No, I haven't. Tell us more. What does it involve? Well, from what I've read, it's a new type of immunotherapy that can actually desensitize people to certain allergens.

I'm telling you, I've been struggling to get my students to engage with the new module on Moodle. I've tried everything from discussion forums to interactive quizzes, but nothing seems to be working. Ah, come on, it's not that bad, is it? You're just having a tough time getting them to adjust to the new format. I've found that if you make the activities more relevant to their interests, they're more likely to participate. But that's just it, I have made it relevant. I've used real-world examples and case studies, but they just don't seem to be bothered. And to make matters worse, the IT department has been having some issues with the Moodle server, so it's been down a few times, which hasn't helped. Hmm, that's frustrating. Have you tried using some of the other features on Moodle, like the gamification tools or the peer assessment modules? Sometimes, giving them a bit of competition or autonomy can motivate them to take part. Actually, I haven't tried the gamification tools yet, but that's a great idea. I'll have to look into it. But I'm not sure about the peer assessment modules. I've had mixed results with those in the past. The students either take it too seriously and get stressed out, or they don't take it seriously enough and just give each other high marks without actually providing any useful feedback. Yeah, I can see how that would be a problem. But maybe you could try using it in a more low-stakes way, like a practice exercise or a formative assessment? That way, they can get used to giving and receiving feedback without it affecting their grades. That's not a bad idea. I might try that. But what about you, how's your teaching going? You've been using Moodle for years, what are some of your favorite features? Well, I've always been a fan of the wiki tool. I find it's a great way to get students to collaborate on a project and create a shared resource. And I've also had good luck with the database module, which allows students to create and manage their own databases. Oh, I've never used the wiki tool before. How do you find it works in practice? I'm telling you, I'm still feeling the effects of that long-haul flight. I swear, my body thinks it's still in a different time zone. I know what you mean. I've been there too. Mum, it's so great to be back home. I've missed your cooking so much. What's for lunch today? Ah, darling, I'm glad you're home too! I was thinking of making some of your favorite fish and chips.
