Do you remember when I went to Australia and had that terrible jet lag? Oh, yes, you were exhausted for days. But you're looking much better now. By the way, have you started thinking about moving your stuff into the new flat? We should make a list of all the things you need to take with you. Yeah, I've been thinking about it. Let me get a pen and paper, and we can start making that list. Oh, and I almost forgot to tell you, Emily and I have been talking about getting married next year. That's wonderful news, sweetie! I'm so happy for you both. We'll have to start planning the wedding soon. But first, let's focus on getting you settled into your new place. What's the plan for the furniture and all that? Well, I was thinking of keeping some of the old furniture from my previous flat, but I'll need to get some new stuff too. And I'll need your help with moving everything. Maybe we can ask some friends to lend a hand as well. Of course, darling. We'll get it all sorted out. Now, let me tell you, I had the most interesting conversation with your aunt the other day. She was saying that she saw a program about weaver fish and how they can be quite venomous. Really? I didn't know that. I've always loved learning about different types of fish. Maybe we can watch that program together later. But anyway, back to the moving list... what do you think I should prioritize? Well, let's see... you'll need to pack all your clothes and kitchen utensils, and don't forget to arrange for the internet and electricity to be set up at the new flat. And have you thought about how you'll get all your stuff there? We could rent a van or something.

Ah'm tellin' ye, pet, ah've been meanin' to get some more plants for t'house. It's a grand way to purify t'air and boost me mood, y'knaa? You and your plants, love. I'm not complaining, though. The living room does look lovely with all the greenery. What type were you thinking of getting this time? Well, ah was thinkin' maybe some snake plants or a peace lily. They're low maintenance, so they're perfect for us since we're both busy with work and whatnot. Plus, they're great at removin' toxins from the air, which is a bonus considerin' the petrol crisis that's goin' on. That's a great point. I hadn't thought of that. And speaking of things that are a mess, have you seen the latest news about the NHS? The staff shortages are gettin' out of hand, and it's affecting patient care. Aye, ah saw that. It's a cryin' shame, is what it is. The NHS is one of the best healthcare systems in the world, and it's bein' stretched to the limit. We need to do somethin' to support the staff and ensure patients are gettin' the care they need. It's not just about throwin' more money at the problem, either – we need a proper plan to address the root causes of the shortages. I couldn't agree more. It's the same with the A-Level reforms they're proposin'. They're tryin' to simplify the system, but I think it's just goin' to end up bein' more confusing for the students. And what's the point of changin' the system if it's not goin' to address the real issues, like lack of funding for schools and unequal access to resources? Exactly! And it's not just about the students, either. The teachers are the ones who are goin' to have to deal with the fallout from these changes. They're already overworked and underpaid, and this is just goin' to add more stress to their lives. By the way, when was the last time you had a haircut? You're lookin' a bit shaggy, if ye don't mind me sayin' so. Ah, cheers, love. I was thinkin' of gettin' a trim this weekend, actually. Maybe I'll try out that new barber shop on Mill Road. I've heard good things about it.

Ah'm tellin' thee, I'm so done wi' people smokin' outside t'uni buildings. It's like, can't they just go somewhere else? I'm tryin' to get to me lectures without breathin' in a load of second-hand smoke. I know what you mean, it's really annoying. I've been tryin' to avoid walkin' past the smoker's corner near the library, but it's like, they're everywhere! Have you noticed how many people smoke at our uni compared to back home in Cambridge? Aye, it's mental! I've been thinkin' about startin' a petition to get them to move the designated smokin' areas to somewhere less crowded. Maybe near the car park or sommat. What do you think, lasses? That's a great idea, pet! I'm so sick of smokin' bein' glorified, especially among young people. It's like, don't they know how bad it is for their health? And it's not just the health risks, it's the environmental impact too. Exactly! And it's not just about the smokers themselves, it's about the people around them who have to breathe in the smoke. I've got a mate who's got asthma, and it's a right nightmare for her when people smoke near her. Yeah, and it's not just about individual health, it's about the broader social implications. I mean, have you guys been readin' about the feminist perspectives on smokin' and how it's been marketed towards women as a form of liberation? Oh, aye! I did a essay on that last semester, and it's really interestin' to see how the tobacco industry has targeted women with their advertising. It's like, they're tryin' to make smokin' seem empowering, but really it's just a way to control people's habits and make a profit. That's so true. And speakin' of profits, have you guys heard about the new budget cuts at our uni? I'm gettin' a bit worried about how it's gonna affect our courses and our future job prospects. Ah, don't even get me started on that! I'm already stressed about gettin' a job after graduation, and now they're cuttin' funds for our departments? It's like, what are we supposed to do? I know, it's really unsettlin'. But we should try to stay positive and focus on what we can control.

I'm telling you, it's so much harder to end a friendship than a romantic relationship. At least with a partner, there's a clear-cut way to break up, but with friends, it's all so... ambiguous. I know what you mean. I've been thinking about this a lot lately, especially with some of the friends I've made through work. We've grown apart, but I still feel guilty about not making an effort to see them as much. Exactly! And it's not like you can just sit them down and say, "Look, I don't want to be friends with you anymore." That's just cruel. But at the same time, you can't keep pretending that everything is fine when it's not. That's what I've been doing, to be honest. I've been putting off meeting up with them, hoping that they'll just get the hint and stop inviting me out. But it's not very fair to them, is it? No, it's not. I think the key is to just be honest, but also kind. You can say something like, "I've been really busy lately, and I need to prioritize my own relationships and hobbies." That way, you're not blaming them or making them feel like it's their fault. That makes sense. But what if they keep pushing for you to hang out? Like, what if they're really clingy or don't take the hint? Well, that's where it gets tricky. I think in those cases, you just have to be firm but polite. You can say, "I appreciate the invitation, but I don't think we're as close as we used to be, and I need to focus on my own life right now." It's okay to set boundaries and prioritize your own needs. I see what you mean. It's like, you can't pour from an empty cup, right? You need to take care of yourself before you can be a good friend to anyone else. Exactly! And it's not like you're being selfish or anything. You're just being realistic about what you can handle and what's healthy for you. I mean, I've had to phase out a few friends in the past, and it's always hard, but it's also kind of liberating.

Blimey, Mum, this roast chicken is smashin'! You've outdone yourself this time. Oh, thank you, dear. I'm glad you're enjoying it. I was thinking of trying out a new recipe, but I decided to stick with the classic one. By the way, how's university been treating you? You haven't told me much about it lately. It's been alright, I s'pose. Just been keepin' busy with coursework and whatnot. I had a bit of a rough patch with me dissertation, but I've been workin' on gettin' it back on track. I've been gettin' some help from me tutor, so that's been a big help. Ah, I'm glad to hear that. I was a bit worried when you said you were strugglin' with it. You know, your father was always good at writin' and research. I'm sure you get that from him. Speaking of which, have you spoken to your sister lately? I haven't heard from her in ages. Yeah, I spoke to her last week, actually. She's doin' alright, just been keepin' busy with work and her own thing. She's still thinkin' about movin' to Manchester, but she's not sure yet. I reckon she'll make the right decision, though. That's good to hear. I've been meanin' to give her a call, but I've been so caught up with me own work. I've been preparin' for an exhibition at a local gallery, and it's been takin' up a lot of me time. Oh, that sounds excitin'! What kind of art are you displayin'? Are you still doin' those watercolors you're so fond of? Yes, I am. I've been workin' on a series of watercolors inspired by me travels to Italy. I've always loved the light and the colors there, and I've been tryin' to capture that in me paintings. I think it's some of me best work, if I do say so myself. I'm sure it is, Mum. You're always so talented when it comes to art. I remember when I was a kid, you used to take me to all those art museums and galleries. You'd spend hours explainin' all the different techniques and styles to me. I didn't always understand it, but it was always fascinatin' to listen to you. Ah, those were good times.

I'm telling you, it's all about timing when it comes to eating before the gym. I mean, I used to go to the gym all the time when I was working, and I'd always make sure to have a light snack about an hour before. You don't want to be too full, or you'll feel sick while you're on the treadmill. Yeah, that makes sense. I've been trying to get into a routine with my workouts, but it's hard when you're traveling like this. I mean, we're on a campervan journey, for crying out loud! It's not exactly easy to find a gym in the middle of nowhere, Poland. Fair point. But we're not exactly in the middle of nowhere, are we? We're on our way to Tarnow, and I'm sure they have a lovely gym there. Besides, it's not just about the gym. It's about being mindful of your body and what you put into it. Eating before a workout gives you energy, you know? Absolutely. And speaking of energy, how's your driving going? You've been behind the wheel for a while now. Do you need me to take over? Oh, no, I'm fine, thanks. I'm actually enjoying the drive. The scenery is lovely, and it's nice to have some time to think. Although, I have to say, I'm a bit concerned about the time. We don't want to arrive in Tarnow too late, do we? Don't worry, we'll be fine. We've got plenty of time. And besides, it's not like we have a strict schedule to keep. We're on holiday, after all! Although, I did promise my sister I'd call her today. Do you mind if I make a quick phone call? Not at all, dear. Go ahead. I'll just keep driving and enjoy the view. You know, it's funny. As an English person, I sometimes feel like we're a bit... invisible when we're traveling abroad. Like, people don't always notice us or realize where we're from. Hey, sis... yeah, we're on our way to Tarnow... Okay, got it. Sorry about that. Where were we? Ah yes, being English. I know what you mean. Sometimes I feel like people have certain expectations of us, you know?

Ah'm tellin' thee, I've just got t'most beautiful hand-thrown mugs from that new pottery shop in Saltaire. They're perfect for a cuppa on a cold mornin' like this. Would yer like another cup, love? Aye, that'd be lovely, thank yer. I'm fair clemmed. An' I must say, these mugs are a treat. I've not seen anythin' like 'em since I were a lass. What's t'milk situation like, by t'way? I hope we've not run out again. Don't worry, I've got a fresh pint from t'dairy. An' isn't it a grand day out today? T'sun's shinin' an' t'birds are singin' their 'earts out. Though, I did see a spider scurryin' across t'window sill earlier. I'm not fond of 'em, but I suppose they're useful for keepin' t'flies down. Ugh, don't mention spiders! I had one in t'bath last week an' I near had a fit. But, aye, t'weather's been lovely lately. I've been gettin' out into t'garden a lot, doin' some tidying up an' whatnot. Though, I did have a bit of a scare t'other day when I were prunin' t'roses. I got me finger caught in t'pruning shears. Silly old woman, I am. Oh, that sounds painful! Are yer okay now? An' speakin' of t'garden, I were thinkin' of puttin' in some new flower beds. Maybe some violas an' pansies. What do yer think? An' by t'way, have yer heard from our friend, Margaret, lately? I've not seen 'er since t'power cut last week. Ah, yes, Margaret! She's doin' all right, I think. She were sayin' sommat about gettin' some new decorations for 'er livin' room. An' I'm sure she'd be happy to give yer some advice on t'gardenin' front. She's always been good with flowers. An' speakin' of which, have yer seen t'birds that've been visitin' our garden lately? I've seen some lovely robins an' blue tits. Aye, I've seen 'em! They're a right treat, aren't they? An' I've been thinkin' of puttin' up a new bird feeder. Maybe one of them fancy ones with t'weight-activated perches. An' did yer hear about t'festival that's comin' up in Ilkley? I were thinkin' of takin' a trip out to see what's what. Ilkley festival? I'd not heard about that. What's it all about, then?

I'm so excited for our holiday next week, Mum. I've been counting down the days until we leave for Spain. I know, sweetie, me too. I've been looking at the weather forecast and it's supposed to be lovely and sunny. Just what we need after a long winter. Aye, it'll be grand to get some warm weather. I've been practicing me guitar and I'm thinking of bringing it along to play some tunes on the beach. Oh, Dad, that would be so embarrassing! But also kind of cool, I suppose. Can you teach me some chords before we go? That's a great idea, dear. Your father can teach you some songs to play together on the beach. It'll be a lovely way to spend some quality time together as a family. Ah, I'd like that, love. I've got a few easy ones that you can learn quickly. We can practice together tonight after dinner. Yeah, that sounds like fun. So, Mum, have you spoken to Emma and Mike about meeting up with us while we're on holiday? They're always talking about visiting Spain. Actually, I was thinking of sending them a message today to see if they're free to meet up. It would be great to catch up with them and show them around the area we're staying in. Aye, it's always good to have some friends to share the experience with. And Emma and Mike are good sorts, they'll fit right in with our clan. Yeah, I love Emma's stories about her job. She's always got some funny anecdote to share. And Mike's always making us laugh with his jokes. That's true, dear. They're a great couple and we always have a good time when we're together. I'll send them a message later and see what they say. So, has everyone got their packing lists ready? We don't want to forget anything important. I've got mine started, but I'm not sure what to pack yet. Mum, can you help me decide what clothes to bring? Of course, sweetie. Let's take a look at the forecast again and see what activities we have planned, then we can decide what you'll need to pack. And don't forget to pack your sunscreen and a good book for the beach.

Oh my god, I'm still thinking about that film we just watched, "10 Things I Hate About You". I love Heath Ledger, he's so fit! I know, right? I've seen it like, five times already. I love the scene where he sings "Can't Take My Eyes Off You" to Julia Stiles' character. It's so romantic! Yeah, that's my favourite part too! I wish someone would do that for me at school. Do you think anyone at our school could be that romantic? Ha! I doubt it. Most of the guys at our school are just interested in football and videogames. I don't think they'd even think of doing something like that. Ugh, don't even get me started on the guys at our school. I'm so over them. So, have you started thinking about what you want to do after we finish our GCSEs? Yeah, a bit. I'm thinking of taking A-levels in English, history, and psychology. What about you? Have you thought about what subjects you want to take? Yeah, I'm thinking of taking English, drama, and art. I love creative subjects, and I think they'd be really fun to study. Do you think we'll be able to get into the same sixth form college? I hope so! It would be great if we could stay together. We should start looking into it soon, so we can make sure we get into the same one. Oh, and speaking of fun things, have you forgotten about our trip to London next month? No way! I've been counting down the days until we go. I'm so excited to see the sights and go shopping. We should make a list of all the things we want to do and see while we're there. Definitely! I was thinking we could visit the Tower of London, and then go to Covent Garden and do some shopping. And of course, we have to see a West End show. What do you think? That sounds like an amazing plan! I'd love to see a musical, maybe something like "Wicked" or "Les Mis". Do you think we could get tickets? We should be able to, if we book them soon. I'll ask my mum to look into it for us. Oh, and I just remembered, we need to do our homework for English tomorrow.

I'm tellin' ya, I don't understand this Facebook business. My granddaughter's always on about it, but I just don't see the point. What's wrong with a good ol' chat on the phone or a face-to-face conversation, eh? Oh, come on, dear. It's just a way for people to stay connected. I've got all my old friends from Harrow on there, and we have a right old natter. You should give it a try, you never know, you might enjoy it. Actually, I think it's quite interesting. As a lecturer, I've done some research on how social media affects people's behavior and mental health. It's fascinating to see how people present themselves online versus in real life. But, I have to say, I've been noticing some worrying trends, especially among young people. Yes, I've seen that too. The pressure to present a perfect online persona can be overwhelming. And it's not just young people, I've had students in their 30s and 40s who struggle with the constant need for validation and likes. It's like they're trying to curate this perfect image, but it's not real. That's just it, isn't it? It's all a bit fake. I mean, who posts about their dirty laundry or their arguments with their spouse? Nobody, that's who. It's all just a big show. Well, I think it's nice to share the positive things in life. And it's a great way to keep up with what's going on in people's lives. Like, I've got a friend who's been struggling with OCD, and she posts about her experiences and how she's coping. It's really helpful to see that she's not alone. Ah, yes, OCD is a really interesting topic. I've had students who have struggled with it, and it's amazing to see how they've learned to manage their symptoms and live with it. But, it's also important to remember that everyone's experience is different, and what works for one person might not work for another. And it's not just OCD, is it? I mean, there are so many other conditions that people struggle with. Like, I've got a colleague whose child had chicken pox recently, and it was a right old ordeal.

I'm tellin' you, our holiday to Germany last year was just the best. The food, the scenery, the people... everything was just so lovely. And you know what really made it special? The little village we stayed in, it was like steppin' back in time. Oh, I'm so jealous! I've always wanted to visit Germany. What made you decide to go there? Well, my husband, John, he's always been fascinated by the history and culture of the place. And I have to say, it was really interesting to learn about it all. We even took a trip to the Neuschwanstein Castle, it was just breathtaking. Ah, yes! I've been there too, many years ago. It's a beautiful place, isn't it? And the Germans, they're such friendly people. I was there on a business trip, but I managed to sneak in a bit of sightseeing. I've been practicin' my German, actually. I've been usin' this language learnin' app on my phone. It's really helpful, but I have to say, I'm strugglin' a bit with the accent. Ah, don't worry about the accent, love! You'll get the hang of it. I've got a mate who's German, and he's always laughin' at my attempts to speak the language. But he says it's the effort that counts, not the accent. Speak of the devil, I was just thinkin' about the old days, when I used to work in Germany. I had a little Volkswagen Beetle, and I used to drive all around the countryside, explorin' all the little villages and towns. Those were the days, eh? Oh, that sounds like so much fun! I've always loved drivin' in foreign countries, it's such an adventure. Although, I have to say, the last time we went to France, we got lost in the countryside for hours. We were laughin' and joke-in' about it, but really, we were gettin' a bit worried. I can just imagine! You and John, bickering away in the car, tryin' to find your way back to civilization. Ah, yes, I remember those days. Although, I have to say, I was always the one doin' the navigatin' on our family holidays. My wife, she's not exactly the best at readin' maps. I'm the same! I get lost just walkin' down the street.

I'm telling you, their new album is a game-changer. I've had it on repeat since it came out. The way the drummer switches between rhythms is insane. I know, right? I've been listening to it non-stop too. I've even tried to learn some of the beats on my own kit. It's not easy, let me tell you. I can imagine. I've always been impressed by your drumming skills, though. You should start a band again. We could use some new music in our lives. I don't know, man. I've been pretty busy with work at the restaurant. But maybe I'll think about it. We could get Alex to join in on guitar and see what happens. That's a great idea! Alex is a talented musician. I'm sure he'd be up for it. We should give him a call and see what he thinks. Definitely. So, how's life been treating you? How's the job hunt going? I'm starting to think I should take on an internship to get some more experience. That's not a bad idea. I've heard internships can be really valuable for getting your foot in the door. What kind of internship are you thinking of doing? Well, I'm not entirely sure yet. I've been looking into a few different options, but I'm open to suggestions. Do you know of any companies that might be hiring interns? Actually, my cousin's company might be looking for someone. I can ask him about it if you'd like. It's not directly related to music, but it could be a good opportunity. That would be great, thanks! I'd really appreciate it. So, how's work been at the restaurant? Any new recipes you're working on? Always! The chef is constantly coming up with new ideas, and I get to be his guinea pig. But seriously, it's been good. We've had some positive reviews lately, and the atmosphere's been great. You should come in and check it out sometime. I'll definitely have to do that.

Ah'm tellin' thee, it's grand to get out o' t'house for a bit, int it? How's yer coffee, lad? It's alright, mam. Not as good as t'one we get at home, though. Not really, just school and then t'domino drive at t'community centre on Friday. You comin'? Aye, course ah am! Ah love a good domino drive. Reminds me o' when ah were a lass, playin' with me mates at t'local club. We should make a day of it, actually. We could go into Durham first, do some shopping, and then head to t'domino drive. Sounds like a plan, mam. What do we need to get from t'shops? Let me check t'shopping list... Ah, yes! We need to get some more coffee, and some bread for t'weekend. And don't forget, we need to pick up some new beds and sleeping bags for t'summer holiday. Oh, yeah! Ah almost forgot about t'holiday! Where are we goin' again? Ah, ye'll just have to wait and see, lad! But ah will say it's goin' to be a lovely spot, near t'coast. Anyway, it's quite busy in here today, int it? And t'noise from t'drive-through is dreadful! Tell me about it! Ah can barely hear meself think! Ah know, it's like they're tryin' to drown us out! Oh, and ah just got a text from yer dad. He's comin' home early from work today, so we'll have to celebrate with a nice dinner. Yes! Ah love it when we have family dinners! Ah, me too, pet. Ah, and speakin' o' celebrations, have ye heard about t'loyalty promotion at t'chemist's? If ye spend a certain amount, ye get a free gift! Nah, mam, ah don't really care about that. Oh, alright, lad! Ah just thought ah'd mention it. Ah, ye know, this restaurant is in a great location, int it? Just off t'motorway, and close to Newcastle. Aye, it's spot on, mam. Ah love comin' here for a coffee. Ah, me too, pet. Ah, and ah heard on t'news t'other day that there's a new business startin' up in t'area. Some entrepreneurs are openin' a new sportin' goods store. Oh, that sounds cool! Ah might have to check it out.

I'm so glad you could make it down to Sussex, mate. It's been ages since we last caught up. How's life as an Assurance Analyst treating you? Ah, you know, it's been keeping me busy, but I'm not complaining. I've been meaning to ask, how's the English Language Instructor gig going? Still enjoying it? Yeah, it's great. I love it. It's been too long since we've all had a chance to catch up. By the way, have you noticed how many colloquialisms we use when we're talking to each other? Yeah, it's easy to lose track of people when you're busy with work and life. But it's great that you're making an effort to stay in touch. I've been trying to get back into a routine of doing chores and sorting out my finances. It's not the most exciting thing, but it needs to be done. Tell me about it. I've been trying to get my head around our joint bank account and making sure we're not overspending.

I'm telling you, Sarah, it's been a tough few months. Losing my aunt to cancer was a real blow. I'm still trying to come to terms with it, to be honest. Oh, Emma, I'm so sorry. I can only imagine how you must be feeling. Cancer is just a dreadful disease, isn't it? It seems like it's everywhere these days. I've got a friend at work who's going through chemo at the moment, and it's just heartbreaking to see her like that. Yes, it's just terrible. And the thing is, my aunt was only 65. She was far too young to go. I keep thinking about all the things she'll miss out on now - my kids growing up, our family gatherings... it's just not fair. I know what you mean. My mum's been having some health issues lately too, and it's made me realize just how precious life is. We have to make the most of every day, don't we? I've been trying to get her to see a doctor about her mental health, to be honest. She's been struggling with anxiety and depression, and I think it's really taking a toll on her physical health as well. Absolutely. Mental health is just as important as physical health, but sometimes I think we forget that. I've been trying to prioritize my own self-care lately, what with running my own business and looking after the kids. It's not always easy, but I know it's essential. Have you noticed any changes in your mum's behavior that might suggest she's struggling with her mental health? Well, she's been withdrawning from social events and activities she used to enjoy, and she's been having trouble sleeping. She's also been experiencing a lot of physical symptoms like headaches and stomach problems, which I think are related to her anxiety. I've been trying to encourage her to talk to someone about it, but she's been resistant to the idea. I see. It can be really tough to get someone to open up about their mental health, can't it? But it's great that you're supporting her and encouraging her to seek help. Maybe we could suggest she talk to a therapist or counselor? Sometimes just having someone to talk to can make all the difference.

I'm telling you, it's getting more competitive out there for the kids. My marketing business has been getting a lot of requests from schools to help with their social media presence. What do you mean, auntie? Like, how are schools using social media? Well, they're trying to attract more students and show off their facilities. It's all about presentation these days. Although, I have to say, I did see a bloke the other day wearin' a shirt with a picture of a cat on it... that was a bit too much, even for me.

Ey up, Grandma! It's great to see thee. I've been lookin' forward to comin' over all week. How've you been? Ah, hello love! I've been doin' all right, considerin' me age. It's always nice to have some company, especially from me favourite grandson. Now, would you like a cup of tea and a biscuit? Aye, that sounds grand, thanks! So, what's been goin' on in t'world of politics, then? I've been hearin' a lot about it at school. Oh, you know, same old, same old. Politicians makin' promises they can't keep and linin' their own pockets. I'm tellin' you, love, it's enough to make your blood boil. I remember when I was your age, we had real leaders, like Winston Churchill and Clement Attlee. They knew how to run a country. Yeah, I know what you mean, Grandma. It seems like they're all just out for themselves nowadays. But what about this new party that's been gettin' a lot of attention? The one with the young leader? You mean the Liberal Democrats? Your grandad always said that you can't run a country on good intentions alone. But, Grandma, isn't that the problem? All the old parties are just stuck in their ways and won't listen to new ideas. Maybe we need someone who's willin' to think outside the box and try sommat new. I suppose that's a fair point, love. But you have to be careful what you wish for. I remember when Thatcher came in, everyone thought she was goin' to be the saviour of the country, but she ended up devastatin' the North. We can't afford to make mistakes like that again. Aye, I know what you mean. It's a right mess, isn't it? But I reckon we should at least give the new party a chance. They might surprise us. Well, I suppose it's worth a try, love. But I'm not holdin' me breath. Now, would you like another biscuit? I've got some lovely shortbread that I made meself. Thanks, Grandma! You're the best. So, what do you think about this Brexit business, then?

Ah, Granny, it's great to have you over for dinner. The kids are always excited to see you. Thank you, dear. It's lovely to be here. I must say, the dinner table looks beautiful. Although, I do think the kids could use a refresher on their dinner table manners. Oh, Granny, do we have to? Yes, you do, young man. It's essential to learn how to behave at the dinner table. Your mother and I will have to work on that with you. Don't worry, Granny. We've been trying to teach them, but it's an ongoing process. Yes, and it's not just the kids. I'm sure I could use a refresher myself. So, Granny, what's the most important thing to remember about dinner table manners? Well, first and foremost, it's to keep your elbows off the table and your hands visible. And, of course, wait for everyone to be served before you start eating. Oh, Granny, can we talk about something else? Like the blood moon that's happening next week? Ah, yes, the blood moon. That's a fascinating topic. What would you like to know about it, dear? Everything! I've been reading about it online, but I want to hear it from you. Well, I'll do my best to enlighten you. The blood moon is a lunar eclipse, which occurs when the Earth passes between the sun and the moon, casting a shadow on the moon's surface. Wow, Granny, you're a wealth of knowledge. Yes, and it's great that you're so interested in sharing your knowledge with the kids. It's my pleasure, dear. Now, let's talk about family meals. I've been thinking, we should have more regular family dinners, like we used to when your mother was growing up. That's a great idea, Granny. We should definitely make more of an effort to have family meals together. Yeah! And can we have them at Fitzgeralds Park? That would be so much fun! Well, we'll have to see about that, dear. But I do think it's a lovely idea to spend more time together as a family. And I've been thinking, Granny, since you're so great with the kids, maybe you could babysit for them more often? That would give us a break, and the kids would love spending more time with you.

I'm telling you, the Scottish referendum has got everyone talking. I was discussing it with my colleague, Mrs. Jenkins, the other day, and she's absolutely convinced they'll vote for independence. Ah, I've been following it closely too. I think it's a tough call, but I'm not sure they'll go for it in the end. My niece lives in Edinburgh, and she says the atmosphere is quite divided. By the way, how's Mrs. Jenkins doing? I haven't seen her since the family gathering last year. Oh, she's doing all right, I suppose. Still going strong, even if she can be a bit of a handful at times. You know, I had a bit of a job interview at a new school last week, and I was thinking about what she would say if she knew I was considering leaving my current position. A job interview, you say? What made you decide to look for a new position? You've been at that school for years, haven't you? Yes, I have. It's just that, well, the bureaucracy is getting to me, and I feel like I'm not making as much of a difference as I used to. Plus, the new headmaster is...let's just say we don't see eye to eye. But anyway, enough about that. How's business been treating you? I feel like I haven't seen you as much since you started your own company. It's been keeping me busy, that's for sure. There are days when I wonder why I took the plunge, but overall, it's been a good decision. I get to be my own boss, and I've been able to take on some really interesting projects. My daughter's been a big help, too. She's been doing some work for me on the side, and it's been great to have her on board. That's fantastic! I'm sure she's learning a lot from you. My own daughter's been keeping me on my toes, as well. She's going through a bit of a tough time at the moment, and I'm not sure how to support her. Being a parent is never easy, is it? No, it's not. But we do the best we can, and that's all anyone can ask for.

I'm tellin' ya, Dad, I had the best fish and chips at that new place in Bedford last week. You should totally take Ann there for lunch sometime. Oh, that sounds lovely, Aaron! I do love a good plate of fish and chips. What made it so special, dear? Well, they had this massive cod fillet, and it was cooked to perfection. Not too greasy, just right. And the chips were crispy, not all soggy like some places. Yeah, I've been meaning to try that place out. Is it the one near the river? Yeah, that's the one! You should come with me next time, and we can grab lunch together. Alright, alright, let's not get too distracted. We've got a bit of a drive ahead of us, and I don't want to get stuck in traffic. Ann, how was your week? Anything exciting happen? Oh, just the usual, dear. I did start planning our next trip, though. I was thinking maybe we could go to the coast for a weekend? Get some fresh air and walk on the beach. Sounds like a great idea, Mum! I'm in, as long as we can bring the dogs, of course. Yeah, because nothing says relaxation like a couple of energetic dogs running around on the beach. Oh, they're such good boys, though! I'm sure they'll be fine. Well, we'll see about that. So, Aaron, have you given any more thought to that tuition fees issue you were complaining about last week? Yeah, I have. It's just so frustrating, you know? I feel like I'm being priced out of furthering my education. And it's not like I'm asking for much, just a bit of help with the costs. I know what you mean, mate. I've been there myself. But maybe we can look into some options together? I've heard of some schemes that might be able to help. That's very kind of you, dear. I'm sure Aaron would appreciate that. Alright, let's talk about something more pleasant. Who's up for a game night this weekend? We can break out the old board games and have a laugh. Sounds like a plan to me, Dad! I'm always up for a bit of competition. Yeah, I'm in. But don't expect any mercy from me, Aaron.

Ah'm tellin' ye, driving doon this road is a nightmare, especially wi' a' these potholes. It's like they expect us to have suspension made o' rubber or sommat. Aye, tha's reight, lass. I remember when I used to drive doon these roads, it were a lot smoother. But, by 'eck, it's got worse ower the years. I'm surprised yer car's still in one piece. Ha! It's a miracle, int it? Ah've had to get it serviced more times than ah can count. But, anyway, enough about that. How were yer horses doin' when ye last went to visit yer mate's farm? Oh, they were doin' all reight, thanks for askin'. He's got a new batch o' foals, an' they're as cute as buttons. An' his cows are still producin' some o' the best milk in the county, if ah do say so masel'. You're such a farmer at heart, granddad. I'm surprised you didn't become one instead of workin' for BT. Ah, well, someone's got to keep the phones workin', lad. But, between you an' me, ah've always had a soft spot for farm animals. There's sommat about 'em that just gets me, y'know? Aye, ah can understand that. Ah've always loved animals, especially horses. There's sommat so majestic about 'em, int there? Ah used to go ridin' all the time when ah were a lass. Really? I've always wanted to learn how to ride a horse. Do you think you could teach me, Emily? Course ah can, mate! Ah'd be happy to take ye to the stables an' give ye a lesson or two. It's not as hard as it looks, an' once ye get the hang o' it, it's a right laugh. An' don't forget to wear a helmet, lad. Ah don't want ye breakin' yer neck on me watch. Don't worry, granddad, I'll make sure to wear a helmet. So, what's the best way to approach a horse, Emily? Ah've always been a bit nervous around 'em. Well, first o' all, ye've got to make sure ye're calm an' relaxed. Horses can sense when ye're nervous, an' it'll make 'em nervous too. Then, ye've just got to walk up to 'em slowly an' let 'em sniff ye. They've got a great sense o' smell, an' they'll be able to tell if ye're friendly or not.

I'm so glad we're all together for dinner tonight, it's been too long. And I must say, the food is lovely, Speaker_2. You've outdone yourself with the roast chicken. Thank you, Speaker_1! I'm glad you're enjoying it. I was thinking of trying out some new recipes, maybe some healthier options. You know, to help us all get back on track with our exercise routines. Ah, exercise! I've been meaning to start going for walks again, now that the weather's improved. We should all try to get out more, get some fresh air. Remember when we used to go hiking in the lakes? We should do that again soon. That sounds like a great idea, dear. I've been wanting to get back into shape, especially since I've retired from teaching. I find I have so much more time on my hands now. Speaking of which, have you all heard about the new choir that's starting up in Hunsonby? I was thinking of joining, it might be a fun way to meet new people. Oh, that sounds wonderful! I'd love to come with you to the first meeting. When is it again? And how's your family doing, Speaker_1? How's your niece adjusting to her new school? Ah, she's doing all right, I think. Still getting used to the new teachers and all that. But she's a bright girl, she'll settle in soon enough. And actually, that reminds me - I was talking to one of my old colleagues the other day, and they were saying how the school is in need of some new equipment for the maths department. I was thinking, maybe we could all chip in and help out a bit? That's a great idea, Speaker_1. I've been feeling a bit guilty about not being able to contribute much to the community lately, what with being out of work and all. But this could be a good way for me to give back. How much were you thinking of donating? I think that's a wonderful gesture, Speaker_1. And actually, it ties in nicely with something I've been wanting to discuss with you all. I've been thinking of volunteering at a local charity that helps underprivileged kids with their education. Maybe we could all get involved, make it a family affair?

Alright kids, settle down and eat your dinner. We can talk about parent's evening while we eat. So, Emily, how did you feel about what your teacher said about your maths work? I don't know, Mummy. I just don't get it sometimes. Fractions are really hard. I know it can be tough, but you're doing your best and that's all that matters. We can practice together at home if you'd like. And how about you, Jack? What did your teacher say about your work? She said I'm doing really well with my reading, but I need to work on my writing. And she said I'm very good at maths! Yeah, Jack's really good at maths! I wish I was as good as him. Well, everyone has their strengths and weaknesses, and that's what makes us all different. It's great that Jack is doing well with maths, but Emily, you're very good at reading and writing. Maybe Jack can help you with maths and you can help him with writing. Yeah! I can help Emily with maths. And Emily can help me with writing. Exactly! Teamwork makes the dream work. Now, who's excited about World Book Day tomorrow? We need to finalize your costumes. I am! I'm going to dress up as Matilda. I love her because she's so brave and clever. And I'm going to dress up as Charlie from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. I wish I could find a golden ticket! Well, you never know, maybe you'll find a golden ticket tomorrow! And speaking of fun things, I was thinking we could go to the circus next weekend. Who would like that? Yes! I love the circus! Can we see the clowns and the elephants? And can we see the acrobats? I want to see them flying through the air. We'll see what we can do. I'll check the program and see what performances they have. Now, let's finish dinner and then we can make some arrangements for after school tomorrow. Emily, you have your maths club, and Jack, you have your football practice. I'll make sure to pick you both up on time. Thanks, Mummy. And can we have a special treat after school tomorrow? We'll see. Maybe we can stop by the ice cream shop on the way home.

I'm tellin' ye, it's great to see the young fella workin' away in the curtain shop. He's got a good head on his shoulders, that one. Oh, I know, isn't he just the most adorable thing? And his way of talkin' is just precious. I mean, who says "mammy" and "daddy" like that anymore? Mammy! Daddy! Can we have cake now? Ah, not just yet, little man. We're still eatin' our dinner. But we will have cake, don't you worry. So, have you given any more thought to the arrangements for Oisin's birthday party? I was thinkin' maybe we could have it at the park, and I could make some of those lovely sandwiches you like. Ah, that sounds like a grand idea, love. And I was thinkin' maybe we could get some of the lads from the rugby team to come and help out. We could even have a wee mini match for the kids. Oh, I'm not sure that's such a good idea, dear. Those rugby players can be a bit...rowdy, can't they? Oh, come on, Mum. It'll be fun, I'm sure. And the kids will love it. Besides, I've got a bit of a connection with the team, bein' the treasurer of the garages and all. I'm sure they'll be happy to lend a hand. The treasurer of the garages? What's that all about, then? Ah, just a wee side project I've taken on. Helps to keep the old brain active, you know? So, have you talked to your step-brother about comin' to the party? I know Oisin would love to see him. Ah, yeah...I haven't had a chance to reach out to him yet, but I will. You know how it is with step-relations...sometimes it's a bit...complicated. Complicated? That's one way to put it. I've always said you should be careful around him, dear. Oh, don't be such a worrier, Mum. We'll be fine. And speaking of bein' fine, has anyone been botherin' you with those charity calls lately? Ah, you have no idea. They're always ringin' up, askin' for money. I've had to get a bit aggressive with them, to be honest. Aggressive? That's not very nice, dear. Maybe you should just tell them you're not interested and leave it at that.

Alrigh' lads, I'm fair excited about this new word game I found oot. It's called Word Chain, an' the goal's to come up wi' words that start wi' the last letter o' the previous word. That sounds like a great game, Anna. I've played something similar before, but I'm not sure I'm as good at it as you are. What's the record for the longest chain you've managed to create? Ah, y'knaa, I've got a pretty good one goin' on wi' me mates from work. We got up to aboot 25 words afore we got stuck. It were a reet challenge, like. But I'm determined to beat that record, y'knaa? I'm intrigued by the idea of a word chain. Can you give me an example of how it works, Anna? Maybe we can have a go at it now and see how far we get. Aye, course I can! Let's say the first word is "cat". Then, the next word has to start wi' "T", like "tiger". After that, the next word's got to start wi' "R", like "rhino". An' so on. It's a grand way to test yer vocabulary, an' it's a lot o' fun, too. That makes sense. I think I'd like to give it a try. Anna, why don't you start us off with a word, and then we can take turns coming up with words that fit the rule? Sounds like a plan, Tom! Alrigh', here's a word to get us started: "house". Now it's yer turn, Alex. Can ye think o' a word that starts wi' "E", the last letter o' "house"? Hmm, that's a good one... How about "elephant"? Does that count? Aye, that's perfect, Alex! "Elephant" starts wi' "E", so that's a great choice. Now it's Tom's turn again. Can ye think o' a word that starts wi' "T", the last letter o' "elephant"? Let me think for a moment... Ah, got it! How about "tornado"? Does that fit the rule? Aye, that's spot on, Tom! "Tornado" starts wi' "T", so that's a grand choice. Now it's my turn again. I need to think o' a word that starts wi' "O", the last letter o' "tornado"... Hmm, this is a tough one... Take your time, Anna. We're not in a rush.

Ey up, it's been ages since we last caught up properly! How's life been treatin' yer? Ah, ya know, same old same old. Just tryin' to get through me coursework and whatnot. How 'bout you? How's the graduate life treatin' yer? It's alright, I s'pose. I've been keepin' busy with a bit of work here and there. But, to be honest, I've been takin' a lot of naps lately. I swear, I've been sleepin' more than a baby! That's nothin' new, though! You've always been a bit of a sleepyhead. I'm surprised you don't have a PhD in napping by now! Hey, watch it! I'm just conservin' me energy, that's all. So, what kind of music have you been listenin' to lately? I feel like we haven't had a proper music chat in ages. Oh, I've been gettin' into a lot of indie stuff. You know, the usual – Arctic Monkeys, The 1975... that sort of thing. How about you? Still listenin' to Taylor Swift on repeat? Shut it! I do still like Taylor, but I've been listenin' to a lot of Billie Eilish lately. Her sound's just so unique and refreshing, ya know? Definitely. I've been meanin' to check her out more. I've only heard a few of her songs, but they're all right. Speakin' of which, have you seen Alex lately? I feel like we haven't all hung out together in ages. Actually, I saw him last week. We were out at the pub and he was tellin' us about his new job. He's doin' all right, just a bit stressed out with work and whatnot. But, yeah, we should all get together soon and catch up properly. Definitely. I was lookin' through some old pictures on me phone the other day and I found that one of us from freshman year... Oh God, which one? The one where we're all dressed up in them stupid costumes? No, it was the one where we're all makin' silly faces and poses. You had that ridiculous hairdo goin' on... Oh, shut it! That was just a phase, okay? I was goin' through a bit of an experimental stage, that's all. Oh, experimental stage? You mean like when you decided to dye your hair pink and it ended up lookin' like a failed science experiment?

I'm telling you, it's going to be a right ordeal, this council planning committee meeting. I've been going over the application and I just can't see how they can refuse it. And maybe we could set up a special "vintage" section, with the more expensive items on display. That's a great idea. I'll look into getting the valuations done this week. And in the meantime, we can start sorting through the rest of the items and pricing them up.

I'm so glad we're finally having a chance to catch up, it feels like we haven't talked in ages. How was your day at work? It was alright, I guess. Just the usual chaos on the ward. We're short-staffed at the moment, so it's been a bit of a struggle. But I did have a nice lunch break, I met up with Sarah from school. Oh, how is she? I haven't seen her since we left school. What's she up to these days? She's doing well, just got a new job in marketing. We grabbed some lunch at that new café downtown and caught up on everything. It was really nice to see her. That sounds lovely. I've been meaning to try that café out, how is the food? It's really good, they do a great selection of sandwiches and salads. And the cakes are amazing, I had a slice of lemon drizzle that was just incredible. Mmm, that sounds delicious. I'll have to add it to my list of places to try. So, what's been annoying you lately? I've been wanting to try it out. Sounds like a plan to me. Oh, and I saw that new top you've been eyeing in the shops is on sale now. We should go shopping on Sunday and pick it up. Really? I hadn't seen that it was on sale.

Lah, I'm made up we got all the housework done today, int I? The place is spotless now. Yeah, it's lookin' good, isn't it? I was thinkin' we could get a cleaner in, though. I've got a mate who's been tryin' to quit for ages, too. He's been usin' them nicotine patches and whatnot. Anyway, enough about that. I was thinkin' we could go to that car boot sale at the weekend, yeah? I heard they've got some top deals on old mobile phones and stuff. Ooh, that sounds like a great idea! I love rummagin' through all the old junk and findin' hidden gems. And speakin' of great ideas, I've been readin' this book on NLP and it's got me thinkin' about me own behaviors and habits. You're always readin' about that sorta stuff, aren't you, bein' an assistant psychologist and all? Yeah, somethin' like that. But it's really interestin' stuff. I mean, I still love browsin' through me phone and buyin' stuff, but at least now I'm more aware of me spendin' habits. Online shoppin' addiction, eh? You're such a shopaholic, lah! But seriously, I'm glad you're gettin' it under control. We don't want you breakin' the bank, do we? Speakin' of which, have you seen the news lately? There's been a right lot of crime goin' on in the area, int there?

I'm so glad we're all finally together in one place. It feels like it's been ages since we've had a chance to catch up. How's everyone doing? I'm doing all right, thanks. We've been looking at a few different areas, but we're trying to weigh the pros and cons of each one. You can get any type of cuisine you want, at any time of day or night. I'm a big fan of trying new restaurants and dishes, so I think you'd really enjoy that aspect of living in London. The food was really good, but the service was a bit slow. I think they're still working out some of the kinks, but overall it was a great experience.

I still remember when I first moved to this area in the 1960s. It was a completely different time, wasn't it? I was a young teacher, full of idealism and ready to take on the world. Ah, yes! I know exactly what you mean. I came to this area around the same time, but for a rather different reason. I had an interview to be a dentist, and I was determined to make a good impression. I recall wearing my best suit and trying to look as confident as possible. I'm sure you did, old chap! I, on the other hand, was already working as a teacher when I met my wife. We met at a college social event, and the rest, as they say, is history. But I'm curious, where did you two meet your wives? Oh, I met my husband at a teacher's conference, of all places. We were both attending a seminar on language teaching methods, and we struck up a conversation during the break. It was love at first sight, or so I like to think! Ah, romance was in the air, it seems! As for me, I met my wife while I was doing my postgraduate course in dentistry. It was a bit of a whirlwind romance, I must say. We got married just a few months after meeting, and we've been inseparable ever since. That's wonderful! I've always been fascinated by your story about doing your postgraduate course in Athens, though. Tell us again about the time you arrived just as the dictatorship was starting. Ah, yes, what a tale! I had just arrived in Athens, eager to start my course, when suddenly the city was plunged into chaos. It was 1967, and the military had just taken over. I remember being stuck in my hotel room, wondering what on earth was going on. And to make matters worse, I had to deal with the time change, which completely threw me off. I kept turning up to classes at the wrong time! That's hilarious! I can just imagine you, wandering around Athens, trying to make sense of the situation. But I'm sure it was a bit scary at the time, too. Oh, I'm sure it was. I remember hearing about the coup on the news and being shocked. I'm so glad we're having a lazy day today, Emily. This weather is just dreadful, isn't it? I mean, I know we're in Poland and all, but I didn't expect it to be this gloomy all the time. I'm so glad we decided to meet up for a cuppa, I needed a break from work. How's your studies going, Emily? Still grappling with that thesis of yours? Alright, you two are up early today! Who woke who up? I woke up first! And then I woke up Timmy. Yeah! Emily jumped on my bed and said "Rise and shine!" Oh, Emily, you little monkey! I'm telling you, the state of politics in this country is a mess. I mean, have you seen the latest polls? It's like they're trying to confuse us on purpose. Ah, come on, love. You can't expect things to change overnight. We've been through tough times before, and we'll get through this too. I think they're more like a bunch of headless chickens running around, flapping their wings and making a lot of noise, but not actually getting anything done. I think that's a bit harsh, Auntie. I mean, they're trying to deal with some really complex issues. It's not easy being in their shoes. Ah, but that's just it, dear. They're not even trying to deal with the issues. There's a lovely little pub just up ahead. We can stop there for a bite to eat and stretch our legs. Sounds like a plan to me. And maybe, just maybe, we can discuss something a bit more pleasant...like our family history. I've been meaning to ask you, love, have you made any progress on tracing our ancestors? Ah, yes! I've actually made some fascinating discoveries. Did you know that our great-great-grandfather was a miner in the Rhondda Valley? Whoa, really? I had no idea. That's amazing! I'd love to hear more about it.

...and then, the dragon breathed fire that melted the ice cream truck. Can you imagine how sad the children in the village would be if they couldn't get their favorite treats? That's so funny, Auntie! But what happens next? Does the dragon say sorry? Well, that's a good question. Maybe the dragon realizes what it has done and decides to help the children. It could use its fiery breath to make the most delicious, unique ice cream flavors the village has ever seen. Yeah! And the dragon could have a special power that makes the ice cream never melt! Ooh, that's a great idea, Timmy! We should write that into our story. I think that's a wonderful idea, girls and boys. You know, it reminds me of the stories Helen Moss writes. She has such a vivid imagination and always includes elements of mystery and adventure. Who's Helen Moss? She's an author who writes children's books. We actually met her at the Linton Book Festival last year. She was talking about her latest publication and how she comes up with ideas for her stories. Oh, I liked her books! She read us a story about a secret garden. That's right! And she also talked about how important it is to keep reading and using our imaginations to create our own stories. Maybe one day, you two can be authors and write your own books. Yeah! I want to write a book about dragons and ice cream! Why don't we make some ice cream and then sit down to write our stories? Yay! Ice cream and storytelling! Yes, please! Can we make strawberry ice cream with sprinkles? Of course, we can. Let's get started on our ice cream making adventure, and then we can let our imaginations run wild with our stories. I'm going to write about a dragon that makes ice cream and saves the day! And I'm going to write about a secret garden with a dragon that makes the best ice cream in the world! I can already imagine the wonderful stories you two are going to create. The Linton Book Festival will have to watch out for our future authors!

I'm telling you, I've been considering going vegetarian for months now. All the documentaries I've been watching about animal cruelty and the environment have really made me think about my food choices. I completely understand where you're coming from. I've been a vegetarian for years, and it's been one of the best decisions I've ever made. Not just for the animals, but for my own health and the planet. Have you heard about this new synthetic meat that's been making waves? Ah, you mean shmeat? I've been reading about it, and it's fascinating. The idea that we can create meat in a lab without harming any animals is a game-changer. Although, I'm not sure how I feel about eating something that's been created in a petri dish. Exactly! I'm not sure if I'm ready to take that step yet. But at the same time, I don't want to contribute to the demand for meat that's been produced in inhumane conditions. Do you guys take any vitamin supplements to make sure you're getting enough nutrients on a veggie diet? Yeah, I take a multivitamin every day, just to be safe. But I've also been doing a lot of research on plant-based sources of vitamins and minerals, so I can make sure I'm getting everything I need from my food. It's amazing how much you can get from a well-planned veggie diet. That's really interesting. I've been thinking about taking some supplements too, especially since I've been feeling a bit run down lately. But I've also been wondering, do you think that veggie diets are more expensive than meat-based ones? I feel like all the specialty products and supplements can add up quickly. That's a good point. I think it can be more expensive, but it's also about making conscious choices about what you're spending your money on. For me, it's worth paying a bit more for food that aligns with my values. And it's not just about the food itself, it's about the system that produces it. The meat industry is a massive contributor to oppression and environmental degradation. Absolutely. And it's not just about the meat industry, it's about the entire system of consumption and waste that we're a part of.

I'm so glad we're all together tonight, it feels like we haven't had a chance to catch up in ages. How was your day, love? It was alright, just the usual chaos at work. You know how it is. I did manage to sneak in a bit of lunch at that new café down the street, though. Their sandwiches are quite nice. Ooh, which one did you try? I've been meaning to check it out. Maybe we can help brainstorm after dinner. Sometimes talking through ideas with others can help get the creative juices flowing again. I swear, every time I open the fridge, I'm surprised by something that's been lurking in the back for weeks. We should really make an effort to clean it out more often. Definitely. And while we're on the subject of cleaning, has anyone seen the instructions for the washing machine? I'm convinced I put them in that drawer, but now they're nowhere to be found. I think I might have seen them in the laundry room. Let me go check. You know, it's funny you mention the washing machine. I was talking to my sister the other day, and she was saying how she's been having trouble with hers. Apparently, it's been making this weird noise and she's not sure what's causing it.

...and then I saw the most beautiful set of butterfly forks at the antique shop in town. I couldn't resist buying them, they're just so delicate and intricate. Butterfly forks? What's so special about them, mum? Well, they're a type of fork that was popular in the Victorian era. They have a very distinctive shape, with a long handle and a small, flat head with two prongs. They were used for eating dessert, particularly sweets and cakes. That sounds like a really fancy way of eating cake! Yes, it was! The Victorians loved their formal dining and etiquette, and using the right cutlery for each course was very important to them. I remember learning about the Victorians in history class. We had to observe a 2 minutes silence for Remembrance Day, and it was really hard to stay quiet for that long. Yeah, I know, right? I was dying to make a joke, but I didn't want to get in trouble. Well, I'm glad you both behaved yourselves. Speaking of special occasions, has everyone remembered that it's grandma's birthday next week? Oh, yeah! I was thinking of getting her a card and a small gift. What do you think she'd like? That's very thoughtful of you, sweetie. I think she'd love something personalized, like a photo album or a customized mug. And we should also start thinking about plans for your birthday, which is coming up soon. Ooh, can we have a party? Pleeease? We'll see, darling. Let's discuss it as a family and come up with some ideas. Maybe we can even plan a trip somewhere interesting. Like where? Well, I've always been fascinated by Russia. The history, the culture, the food... it's all so rich and fascinating. Maybe we could plan a trip to Moscow or St. Petersburg someday. Russia? Isn't it, like, really cold there? Yes, it can be quite chilly, especially in the winter. But that's all part of the adventure, isn't it? And think of all the amazing things we could see and experience: the Kremlin, the Hermitage Museum, the Bolshoi Theatre... That sounds amazing! Can we go during the summer, though? I don't want to freeze my butt off. We'll see, sweetie. Let's do some research and plan something that everyone will enjoy. Now, shall we finish supper and then have some dessert?

...and then we can head down to Cornwall for a week. I've always wanted to take you both to St. Ives, the beaches are just beautiful. We can spend our days exploring the coastline and visiting all the little art galleries. Yay! I love the beach! Can we go to the one with the really big sandcastle? I'm not sure about the sandcastle, sweetie, but we'll definitely find some amazing beaches. And we can also visit the Eden Project, you'll love the big domes and all the plants. I want to go on an adventure! Like in the Adventure Island series we've been reading. Well, we can't promise any treasure hunting, but we can definitely have some exciting adventures in Cornwall. Maybe we can even take a boat trip or go hiking. Can we get some pasties? I love pasties! Of course, we'll get some traditional Cornish pasties. But remember, we have to be careful with what we eat, especially with your food intolerance, okay? What's a food intolerance? It means that some foods can make you feel unwell, so we have to avoid them. But don't worry, we'll make sure to pack some special snacks for you. And can we go to the V&A exhibition when we get back? I want to see the big doll's house! We'll see, sweetie. The V&A is in London, so it's a bit of a trek, but maybe we can plan a special day trip. I have to get back to marking exams soon, but I promise we'll make some time for fun things. What's the V&A? It's a big museum in London that has all sorts of amazing things on display, like art and furniture and even toys. They have a huge doll's house that's just incredible. I want to see it! Can we go, pleeease? We'll see, okay? Let's focus on planning our holiday to Cornwall first, and then we can think about other trips. Can we take our books on holiday? Of course, you can take a few of your favorite books, including the Adventure Island series. We can read them together in the evenings. And can we have a picnic on the beach? That sounds like a perfect idea. We can pack a big basket with all our favorite foods and have a picnic on the beach.

I'm telling you, Mr. Johnson is the worst teacher ever. He's always droning on and on about nothing. I fell asleep in his class yesterday. That's nothing, I fell asleep in his class last week and he didn't even notice. I was literally resting my head on the desk and he just kept talking. That's amazing. I know, right? He's like a robot or something. I'm surprised he doesn't just record his lessons and play them back every year. Exactly. And have you started the coursework for history yet? I'm really struggling to get started on it. Yeah, I've started it. It's not too bad, just a lot of reading and note-taking. I'm finding it pretty interesting, though. I mean, who knew that the Treaty of Versailles was so important? Yeah, I know, right? I'm just having trouble getting motivated to do the work. I keep putting it off and now I'm starting to fall behind. You should come over to my house this weekend and we can work on it together. My mom can help us if we get stuck. That sounds like a good idea. Thanks, mate. I owe you one. No problem, happy to help. So, have you heard about the party that Alex is having next weekend? Yeah, I heard it's going to be massive. Everyone's going to be there. Are you going? Yeah, I am. I'm really looking forward to it. I've been biking a lot lately and I'm thinking of riding my bike there. It's not too far from my house. That's a good idea. I might do the same. It'll be a good way to get some exercise before we stuff our faces with food and drink. Exactly. So, have you seen any good movies lately? Actually, I saw the new Marvel movie last weekend. It was really good. I'd recommend it. Nice, I've been wanting to see that. I'll have to check it out. Hey, do you remember when we were in year 9 and Tom had that allergic reaction in class? Oh man, yeah. That was crazy. He swelled up like a balloon. I know, right? It was so scary. Alrigh' pet, how's the traffic lookin' ahead? Should we take the A1 or try the A19? I don't fancy sittin' in traffic all day. Ah, let me check the sat nav. Yeah, it's lookin' pretty congested on the A1, but the A19's not lookin' too bad. We should be okay if we take that route. Sounds like a plan, then. But there's sommat about the strategy of Test cricket that I love. Maybe we can catch a match at the Riverside this summer? That'd be great, actually. I've been meanin' to get back up to the Northeast and visit your family. We should make a weekend of it. That sounds like a crackin' idea! Me mam would love to see you again. And we can take me bike out for a spin along the coast. The views are stunning, especially near Whitby. Oh, that sounds amazing! Just a hybrid, but it's perfect for the trails and roads around here. I've been thinkin' of gettin' a new one, though – sommat with a bit more suspension and better gears. Hmm, yeah, that makes sense. I've got a mate who's into mountain bikin', and he's always goin' on about the importance of havin' the right gear. I'm so down for Chinese food tonight, I've been craving it all day. What do you guys fancy ordering? Ah, nice! I was thinking we could try that new place that just opened up downtown. I've heard great things about it. Ooh, which one is that? I've been meaning to try it out. Is it the one with the crazy noodle dishes? Yeah, that's the one! How about we get the Kung Pao chicken and the beef in black bean sauce? Those are usually pretty spicy. Mmm, that sounds perfect. And we should get some dumplings too. I love their dumplings. Now, who's going to call and place the order? I'll do it. Oh, and should I ask them to deliver or do we want to pick it up? Definitely get it delivered. I'm way too lazy to go out and pick it up.

Yer know, I've 'eard the NHS is goin' through a tough time, lah. Me sister's a doctor in London, and she's always complainin' about the workload and the lack of resources. It's a cryin' shame, int it? Tell me about it! I've been workin' as a nurse practitioner fer years, and I've seen the difference. It's not just the funding, it's the bureaucracy and the red tape. Sometimes I feel like I'm spendin' more time fillin' out forms than actually helpin' me patients. And don't even get me started on the staff shortages! I can imagine, yeah. I've got a lot of respect fer the work yer do, though. I mean, it's not just a job, it's a vocation, int it? Me mam was a nurse, y'know. She always said it was the most rewardin' thing she'd ever done. But, blimey, the hours she used to work! I'm surprised she didn't burn out, lah. Ah, it's a tough job, but it's worth it in the end, y'know? There's nothin' better than seein' a patient recover and knowin' you've made a difference. But, yeah, the hours can be killer. I'm lucky if I get a full night's sleep during the week, haha! Speakin' of which, how's life as a lecturer treatin' yer? How's the academic world? It's got its ups and downs, like any job, I s'pose. I love teachin' and seein' the students progress, but the admin side of things can be a right pain. And the publishin' pressure's always on, y'know? But, I've been lucky enough to get some me research published, and that's always a buzz. I've also been thinkin' about takin' a trip to Finland with the family, have yer ever been? Ooh, Finland? No, I haven't, but I've 'eard it's beautiful! Me neighbour, Mrs. Jenkins, she went there last year and said it was amazin'. She showed me some of the photos, and the lakes and forests looked stunning. You should take yer family, it'll be a great adventure! By the way, how's yer family doin'? How's the little ones? Ah, they're doin' all right, lah. Me eldest is gettin' into that awkward teenager phase, but me youngest is still me little scallywag, always gettin' into trouble, haha!

Ey up, Frank! 'Ow's it goin', mate? I 'eard the council's been causin' a right ol' fuss about the new welfare reforms. What's yer take on it, lah? Ah, John, it's a disaster, int it? I mean, I've lived 'ere all me life, and I've never seen things as tough as they are now. Me grandson's been strugglin' to find work, and 'e's got a family to feed. It's a cryin' shame, so it is. I know, mate. I've been 'earin' the same stories from me own students. It's like the system's designed to keep people down, rather than lift 'em up. I've been teachin' English Lit for years, but it's 'ard to see the relevance when people are strugglin' to make ends meet. Exactly! And it's not just the welfare system, John. The police are always 'arasin' people, too. I've 'eard stories about 'em stoppin' and searchin' youngsters just for walkin' down the street. It's like they're lookin' for trouble. That's a good point, Frank. I've 'eard similar stories. Me own nephew's been stopped a few times, just for bein' in the wrong place at the wrong time. It's a right worry, so it is. But, yer know, I was talkin' to one of me colleagues the other day, and 'e was sayin' that the police are just as frustrated with the system as everyone else. Frustrated? Frustrated?! They're just followin' orders, John! They're not thinkin' about the impact it's 'avin' on the community. I mean, I've lived 'ere all me life, and I've never seen the community as divided as it is now. It's all this immigration business, innit? Ah, now, Frank, I'm not sure I agree with yer on that one, mate. I mean, I've got a lot of students from immigrant backgrounds, and they're some of the hardest-workin' and most talented people I've ever met. We need to be careful not to blame the wrong people for the problems we're facin'. I'm not sayin' that, John! I'm just sayin' that it's all gettin' a bit too much, know what I mean? Me granddaughter's got a mate who's from Poland, and 'e's a top lad, but...but...oh, I don't know, it's just all so complicated, innit?

Alrigh' pet, how's it goin'? I'm starvin'! What's good here for lunch? Haha, hey! I'm good, thanks. I had the chicken sandwich last time and it was lovely. You should try it. Sounds canny, I might just do that. So, how's work been treatin' ye? Any excitin' projects comin' up? Yeah, actually, we're workin' on a new language learnin' platform. I was sayin' how I'm still gettin' used to bein' a Corpus Administrator. Ah, nice! I've been workin' on some corpus-related projects myself. What kind of texts are you addin' to the corpus? Mostly just some new articles and books that have been published recently. Nothin' too out of the ordinary, just tryin' to keep it up to date. That sounds really interesting. I've been meanin' to get in touch with you about potentially collaboratin' on a project. We might be able to use some of the corpus data for our language learnin' platform. That sounds great! I'm telling you, it's been a challenge getting these students to understand the basics of academic writing.
